description: MJ entity-search corpus: Name + Description of Actions, Agents, Prompts, AI Models and Queries from metadata/**, and core entity descriptions from the generated entity JSDoc. Extracted from the repo on 2026-10-12.

documents.text: Autotag and Vectorize Content: Runs MJ's Content Autotagging and/or Vector Embedding pipeline over Content Items. Either step can be toggled independently via the Autotag and Vectorize boolean parameters (both default ON). Operates on the Content Items entity by default. For vectorizing OTHER entities (not Content Items), use Vectorize Entity instead.

Vectorize Entity: Creates and stores vector embeddings for records in one or more MJ entities. Use to enable semantic search over arbitrary entity data. For Content Items specifically, prefer Autotag and Vectorize Content which also assigns tags. Vectors are stored per the entity's configured vector database and embedding model.

Send Single Message: Sends one outbound message (email, SMS, push notification, etc.) via the MJ Communication Framework. The actual channel is determined by the Provider + MessageType parameters — this single action handles all message types the configured provider supports. For bulk send, use a Run View to gather recipients then loop, or use a provider-specific bulk action if available.
Get Weather: Looks up the current weather for a single location, either by city name or by latitude/longitude. Returns current conditions and temperature for a single point in time.
Get Stock Price: Looks up the current price and trading data for a single publicly-traded stock by ticker symbol. US/major-exchange tickers only. Returns the latest price snapshot.
Calculate Expression: Evaluates mathematical expressions supporting basic arithmetic, parentheses, and common math functions
Color Converter: Converts colors between different formats (HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV) and provides color analysis
Text Analyzer: Analyzes text content providing statistics, readability scores, and word frequency analysis
Unit Converter: Converts values between different units of measurement including length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed, and time
Business Days Calculator: Calculates business days between dates, accounting for weekends and holidays. Can add/subtract business days from a date
IP Geolocation: Retrieves geolocation information for an IP address including location, timezone, ISP, and privacy indicators
Census Data Lookup: Retrieves US Census demographic and economic data for a given ZIP code or city/state location

Web Search: Searches the open web through whichever provider the administrator has configured, and returns ranked results with titles, URLs and snippets. This is the provider-neutral entry point: which vendor serves the request (Brave, Tavily, Perplexity, or a fallback when the first choice is rate-limited) is decided by the MJ: Web Search Providers records and their Priority, not by the caller. Use this for any question needing current information from outside this MemberJunction instance. For content MJ holds, use Search instead.

Web Page Content: Fetches the content of a specific URL and converts it to text/markdown/JSON. Use when you already have a URL (from Web Search, a user-supplied link, or an API endpoint) and need its content. Handles HTML, PDF, DOCX, XML, CSV, and JSON automatically with format detection.
URL Link Validator: Validates URLs by checking accessibility, response codes, and performing health checks with detailed status information
URL Metadata Extractor: Extracts comprehensive metadata from web pages including OpenGraph, Twitter Cards, Schema.org structured data, and standard HTML meta tags
QR Code: Generates and reads QR codes with customizable options for size, error correction, and styling

Create Record: Inserts a NEW record into an MJ entity. Use when the record does not yet exist and you need a generated primary key returned. To modify an existing record, use Update Record. To read existing records, use Get Record (single) or Run View (multiple). Accepts any entity in the MJ metadata; respects entity validation and permissions.

Get Record: Retrieves a SINGLE record from an MJ entity by primary key. Use when you already know the exact record's primary key. To find records by other criteria (status, name, date range), use Run View with a filter. To execute a stored, named query, use Run Query. Returns the full record with all fields the user has read permission on.

Update Record: Modifies an EXISTING record in an MJ entity. Use when the record already exists and you know its primary key. To insert a new record, use Create Record. To remove a record, use Delete Record. Only the supplied fields are changed; all other fields are preserved. Respects entity validation, permissions, and audit trails (Record Changes).

Delete Record: Permanently removes a record from an MJ entity. Hard delete — irreversible. For entities that support soft deletes (e.g. setting Status='Archived'), prefer Update Record. To confirm a record exists before deletion, call Get Record first. Respects cascade rules defined in entity metadata.

Apollo Enrichment - Contacts: Enriches contact records with verified email addresses, employment history, and education details using Apollo.io API. Matches contacts by name and email combinations and provides comprehensive contact enrichment.

Apollo Enrichment - Accounts: Enriches account/organization records with company information, technologies used, and associated contacts using Apollo.io API. Processes accounts by domain name and automatically discovers contacts within each organization.
CSV Parser: Parse CSV data into structured JSON with configurable options for headers, delimiters, and data handling
JSON Transform: Transform JSON data using JSONPath or JMESPath expressions for flexible data manipulation
XML Parser: Parse XML data and extract values using XPath expressions with namespace support
Aggregate Data: Perform aggregation operations on data arrays including sum, average, min, max, count, and group by
Data Mapper: Transform data using Nunjucks templates for flexible and powerful data mapping
PDF Extractor: Extract text, metadata, and pages from PDF files
Excel Reader: Read Excel files and convert to JSON with support for specific sheets and ranges
File Compress: Compress or decompress files using ZIP format with configurable compression levels
HTTP Request: Make HTTP requests with full control over headers, authentication, and request options
GraphQL Query: Execute GraphQL queries and mutations with variable support
OAuth Flow: Handle OAuth 2.0 authentication flows including authorization code and client credentials
API Rate Limiter: Add rate limiting to any API endpoint with automatic retry and backoff
Password Strength: Check password strength and generate secure passwords using zxcvbn analysis
Conditional: Execute different actions based on a condition evaluation
Loop: Iterate over collections executing actions for each item with parallel processing support
Parallel Execute: Execute multiple actions in parallel with configurable concurrency and completion modes
Retry: Retry failed actions with exponential backoff and configurable retry conditions
Delay: Add fixed or random delays to workflows for timing control
Slack Webhook: Send messages to Slack channels via incoming webhooks with rich formatting support
Teams Webhook: Send messages to Microsoft Teams channels via incoming webhooks with card formatting
Execute AI Prompt: Execute MemberJunction AI prompts with variable substitution and model overrides

Perplexity Search: Queries Perplexity in one of two modes. 'search' (default) returns structured title/url/snippet web results from Perplexity's /search endpoint - fast and flat-priced. 'answer' returns a synthesised answer with citations from the Sonar models - slower and token-billed.

Gamma Generate Presentation: Generates presentations, documents, or social media posts using Gamma's AI-powered Generations API. Creates professional slides from text input with customizable themes, images, and export formats.
Get Records: Generic action for retrieving multiple records from any entity with filtering and sorting capabilities. Supports SQL WHERE clause filters, ORDER BY sorting, and result limits.

Create Document: Creates a new in-progress document (PDF, DOCX, or XLSX) and returns a handle for incremental building. Use with Add Document Content, Preview Document, Modify Document Section, and Finalize Document to build documents piece by piece across multiple turns.

Add Document Content: Appends content to an in-progress document created by Create Document. Each call creates a new addressable section. Operations include: heading, paragraph, table, list, image, hr, pageBreak, sheet (Excel), formula (Excel).

Preview Document: Returns a summary of an in-progress document's current state: section count, per-section operation counts and content summaries. Use to check what has been built before adding more or finalizing.
Modify Document Section: Replaces or removes a previously-added section in an in-progress document. Section IDs are returned by Add Document Content and Preview Document.

Finalize Document: Renders an in-progress document to its final binary format, saves to MJ Storage, and outputs FileOutput for automatic artifact creation. The document handle is disposed after finalization.
Postal Code Lookup: Looks up city, state, country, and geographic coordinates from a postal code using the Google Geocoding API. Supports international postal codes.
Geocode Address: Converts a free-form address string into structured address components (street, city, state, postal code, country) and geographic coordinates using the Google Geocoding API.
Reverse Geocode: Converts geographic coordinates (latitude/longitude) into a structured address using the Google Geocoding API. Useful for finding the address at a known location.

Validate Address: Validates and standardizes an address using the Google Address Validation API. Returns corrected address fields, deliverability verdict, geographic coordinates, and USPS data for US addresses. Requires the Address Validation API to be enabled in Google Cloud.

Find Candidate Actions: Finds the most relevant actions for a given task using semantic search with embeddings. Returns top N most similar actions based on task description. Used by Planning Designer Agent to discover relevant actions without searching through hundreds of options.

Load Agent Spec: Loads the complete AgentSpec structure for an existing agent by ID. Returns full agent specification including all nested structures: Actions, SubAgents, Prompts, Steps, and Paths. Used by Agent Manager for modification workflow.

Apollo - Search People: Searches Apollo's people database for net-new prospects by organization, title and seniority. Does NOT return emails or phones — that is Apollo's design for this endpoint. At least one filter should be supplied; Apollo accepts a request with none and returns an unhelpfully broad result.

Apollo - Move List Accounts: Moves accounts from one Apollo list to another. Labels are full-replace in Apollo, so the add is performed BEFORE the remove — a failed add can then never strip the source label. Reads page 1 of the source list only; ids not found there are reported in NotOnSourcePage rather than treated as failures.

Apollo - Move List Contacts: Moves contacts from one Apollo list to another. Labels are full-replace in Apollo, so the add is performed BEFORE the remove — a failed add can then never strip the source label. Reads page 1 of the source list only; ids not found there are reported in NotOnSourcePage rather than treated as failures.

Computer Use: Drives a web browser via LLM reasoning over screenshots to accomplish a natural-language goal. Uses a vision-to-action loop: captures screenshots, sends them to a controller LLM that plans browser actions (click, type, navigate, scroll), executes those actions via Playwright, and evaluates progress with a judge LLM. Supports per-domain authentication, domain allow/block lists, and configurable step limits.

Mermaid is a text-based diagram tool that converts markdown-like syntax into rich visualizations suitable for reports, documentation, and AI-generated content.

Create Runtime Action: Creates a new Action record with Type='Runtime'. Create SVG Chart: Generates SVG charts from data using D3. Supports various chart types including bar, line, pie, scatter, and area charts. Designed for AI agents and workflows to create publication-quality visualizations from structured data without writing visualization code.

Create SVG Diagram: Generates SVG diagrams including flowcharts, org charts, and ER diagrams. Uses dagre for directed graph layouts and d3-hierarchy for tree structures. Designed for AI agents and workflows to create publication-quality diagrams from structured data.

Create SVG Infographic: Composes multiple SVG visualizations into a single infographic with grid layout, header, and footer. Takes panels from other SVG actions (charts, diagrams, networks, word clouds) and arranges them professionally. Designed for AI agents to create comprehensive visual reports.

Create SVG Network: Generates SVG network graphs including force-directed layouts, decision trees, and radial networks. Uses d3-force for physics simulations and d3-hierarchy for tree structures. Designed for AI agents and workflows to create publication-quality network visualizations from structured data.

Create SVG Word Cloud: Generates SVG word clouds and tag bars from weighted word lists. Uses d3-cloud for cloud layouts. Designed for AI agents and workflows to create publication-quality text visualizations from data.

Create Entity: Creates a new MemberJunction entity from a fully-formed TableDefinition. Validates authorization then executes the SchemaEngine → RuntimeSchemaManager pipeline. Use this when an agent needs to create a new database table without going through the full conversational Database Designer flow.

Modify Entity: Applies ALTER TABLE changes to an existing MemberJunction entity based on a desired TableDefinition. Diffs the desired state against the current table, generates ALTER SQL, and executes the pipeline.
List My Entities: Returns a list of all MemberJunction entities created by the current user via the Database Designer (based on MJ:UDT:Owner EntitySettings provenance records).
Describe Entity: Returns detailed column-level metadata for a MemberJunction entity. Useful for inspecting an entity's current structure before deciding to modify it.

Validate Entity Schema: Validates a TableDefinition against all Database Designer pre-creation checks (blocked schemas, reserved column names, naming conflicts). Returns a ValidationResult with Valid, Errors, and Warnings. Call this before CreateEntity to surface problems at the UI review step rather than mid-pipeline.

Send Document for Signature: Send one or more documents through a configured signature account/provider (e.g. DocuSign) and create the envelope lifecycle record. Documents are supplied as base64. Optionally links to an originating record (EntityID/RecordID) and an Artifact for provenance.
Get Signature Status: Poll the provider for the current envelope status of a signature request and persist it (including recipient statuses).
Download Signed Document: Download the executed/signed document for a completed signature request and record it as a Signed-role document. Returns the document as base64.
Void Signature Request: Void/cancel an in-flight signature request with a reason.

Execute Agent: Executes a top-level AI Agent by name or ID using the framework's AgentRunner. Only invokable for agents with ExposeAsAction=true. Returns the AgentRunID, final payload, and full AgentResult. Sub-agents (ParentID set) cannot be invoked through this action — run the parent agent instead.

Execute Code: Executes JavaScript code in a secure sandboxed environment. Designed for AI agents to generate and run code for data analysis, transformations, and calculations. Supports lodash, date-fns, mathjs, papaparse, uuid, and validator libraries. No filesystem or network access.

Explore Database Schema: Retrieves comprehensive database schema information using MemberJunction's rich metadata layer. Provides business context, field descriptions, semantic relationships, virtual entities, API settings, and much more beyond raw database schema. Essential for understanding the data model for research purposes.
Run External Change Detection: Executes the External Change Detection process to identify changes in data that bypassed MemberJunction.

Find Candidate Agents: Finds the best-matching AI agents for a given task using embedding-based semantic search. Returns agents ranked by similarity score.

Create Form Contribution: Persists a net-new form contribution: lints the ComponentSpec (must declare componentRole='form-panel' and a formContribution block), inserts a Type='Widget' Component v1.0.0, and creates a Pending, User-scoped MJ: Entity Form Contributions row at the declared slot with any related-grid claim or replacesSectionKey. Returns ALREADY_EXISTS when the caller already has an Active or Pending row with the same ContributionKey — use 'Modify Form Contribution' then. Returns INVALID_CLAIM, before writing anything, when the spec's claim breaks a rule the database enforces (more than one claim). The Component and the row are written in one transaction, so a refused row leaves no Component behind. Scope is always clamped to User.

Modify Form Contribution: Refines an existing form contribution. Pending source + in-place (default) overwrites the draft; Active source (default minor) or any explicit patch/minor/major bump inserts a new Pending Component + row and leaves the source alone (a Pending source being bumped is demoted to Inactive). Refreshes the row's slot/key/claims/title from the spec's formContribution block; an optional Precedence replaces the row's precedence. Acts only on the caller's own User-scope rows: a Role or Global row, or another user's row, returns FORBIDDEN, because shared panels are managed from the form's Manage drawer or Form Builder. Any new row is User scope. Returns INVALID_CLAIM, before writing anything, when the spec's claim breaks a rule the database enforces; the Component and row writes run in one transaction.

Activate Form Contribution Version: Promotes one of the caller's Pending form contributions to Active and demotes the caller's Active row sharing its EntityID and ContributionKey (Component statuses follow: Published / Deprecated). Idempotent on an Active row; NOT_PENDING on an Inactive row. Acts only on the caller's own User-scope rows: a Role or Global row, or another user's row, returns FORBIDDEN, because shared panels are managed from the form's Manage drawer or Form Builder.

Get Form Contributions For Entity: Read-only. Every MJ: Entity Form Contributions row applicable to the caller (User / Role / Global) for an entity, in every status, with component name and version. On an identity or permission entity (MJ: Users, Roles, Authorizations, API Keys and the like) only the caller's own rows apply, as on the form. Apply flows use it to decide Create vs Modify; agents use it to see what already exists. Lists no row, with MetadataContributionsEnabled false, when metadata contributions are switched off (MJ_FORMS_METADATA_CONTRIBUTIONS=false on the server, or the instance configuration Forms.MetadataContributions.Enabled set to false).

Get Form Composition For Entity: Read-only server-side composition of the entity form the caller sees, for agents with no browser context. Returns whether a full custom form renders for them, field sections by CodeGen rule, DisplayInForm related grids with L1 inclusion, the caller's Active metadata contributions as their form draws them (one per key by Precedence then the narrower scope, panels they hid marked Hidden, only their own on an identity or permission entity), and the L3 rule count. Compiled BaseFormPanel contributions are browser-only and are NOT included. The client form context (AppContext.AdditionalContext.Form) is authoritative for the sections the open form draws when present. Lists no contribution, with MetadataContributionsEnabled false, when metadata contributions are switched off (MJ_FORMS_METADATA_CONTRIBUTIONS=false on the server, or the instance configuration Forms.MetadataContributions.Enabled set to false). Returns QUERY_FAILED when any lookup fails.

Get Single Google Forms Response: Retrieves details of a specific Google Form response by its unique response ID. Requires Google OAuth 2.0 authentication with forms.responses.readonly scope. Includes all answers, metadata, and submission timestamps.

Get Google Forms Response Statistics: Calculates comprehensive statistics from Google Form responses including completion rates, response trends, popular answers, and time-based analytics. Requires Google OAuth 2.0 authentication with forms.responses.readonly scope. Useful for dashboards and reporting.

Get Single JotForm Submission: Retrieves details of a specific JotForm submission by its unique submission ID. Includes all answers, metadata, and submission status.

Get JotForm Response Statistics: Calculates comprehensive statistics from JotForm submissions including response counts, trends, popular answers, and time-based analytics. Useful for dashboards and reporting.
Export JotForm Submissions to CSV: Exports JotForm submissions to CSV format for use in spreadsheets, data analysis tools, or archival. Supports custom delimiters and optional metadata columns.

Watch for New JotForm Submissions: Polls JotForm for new submissions since the last check. Returns only new submissions and updates the last checked timestamp. Perfect for triggering workflows, sending notifications, or syncing data to other systems.
Get JotForm Details: Retrieves complete details of a JotForm including title, questions, properties, and settings. Use this to inspect or backup form configurations.

Create JotForm: Creates a new JotForm with specified title, questions, and properties. Supports all JotForm field types including text, email, multiple choice, rating, and more. Returns the new form ID and shareable link.

Update JotForm: Updates an existing JotForm. Supports merging with existing form data to safely update only specified properties, or full replacement mode. Can update title, questions, and properties.

Get SurveyMonkey Responses: Retrieves responses from a SurveyMonkey survey with advanced filtering, pagination, and sorting capabilities. Supports date range filters, status filtering, and automatic pagination through all responses.
Get Single SurveyMonkey Response: Retrieves details of a specific SurveyMonkey response by its unique response ID. Includes all answers, metadata, recipient information, and response timing data.

Get SurveyMonkey Response Statistics: Calculates comprehensive statistics from SurveyMonkey responses including completion rates, response trends, answer distributions, and time-based analytics. Perfect for dashboards, reporting, and data analysis.

Export SurveyMonkey Responses to CSV: Exports SurveyMonkey responses to CSV format for use in spreadsheets, data analysis tools, or archival. Supports custom delimiters, optional metadata columns, and flexible date filtering.

Watch for New SurveyMonkey Responses: Polls SurveyMonkey for new responses since the last check. Returns only new submissions and updates the last checked timestamp. Ideal for triggering workflows, sending notifications, or syncing data to other systems in real-time.

Get SurveyMonkey Details: Retrieves complete details of a SurveyMonkey survey including title, questions, pages, logic, quota settings, theme, and metadata. Use this to inspect survey configurations, backup survey designs, or analyze survey structure.

Create SurveyMonkey: Creates a new SurveyMonkey survey with specified title, pages, questions, and settings. Supports all question types including multiple choice, text, rating, matrix, and more. Returns the new survey ID and collector URLs.

Update SurveyMonkey: Updates an existing SurveyMonkey survey including title, pages, questions, and settings. Use PATCH mode (default) for safe partial updates or PUT mode for complete replacement. WARNING: PUT mode replaces all survey data - pages and questions not included will be deleted.

Get Typeform Responses: Retrieves responses from a Typeform with filtering, pagination, and search capabilities. Supports date ranges, completion status filters, and automatic pagination through all responses.
Get Single Typeform Response: Retrieves details of a specific Typeform response by its unique response token. Includes all answers, metadata, hidden fields, and calculated values.

Get Typeform Response Statistics: Calculates comprehensive statistics from Typeform responses including completion rates, response trends, popular answers, and time-based analytics. Useful for dashboards and reporting.
Export Typeform Responses to CSV: Exports Typeform responses to CSV format for use in spreadsheets, data analysis tools, or archival. Supports custom delimiters and optional metadata columns.

Watch for New Typeform Responses: Polls Typeform for new responses since the last check. Returns only new submissions and updates the last checked timestamp. Perfect for triggering workflows, sending notifications, or syncing data to other systems.
Get Typeform Details: Retrieves complete details of a Typeform including title, fields, logic jumps, settings, theme, and metadata. Use this to inspect or backup form configurations.

Create Typeform: Creates a new Typeform with specified title, fields, and settings. Supports all field types including text, email, multiple choice, rating, and more. Returns the new form ID and shareable link.

Update Typeform: Updates an existing Typeform. WARNING: Uses PUT which replaces all form data - fields not included will be deleted. Set MergeWithExisting=true to safely update only specified properties while preserving others.
Get Typeform Forms: Retrieves a list of all TypeForms for a company including form IDs, titles, and basic metadata. Use this to discover available forms before processing submissions.
Typeform Get File Content: Downloads file content from Typeform using the file URL from response data. Returns file content in base64, text, or binary format with metadata.

Generate Image: Generates or edits images using AI image generation models (OpenAI GPT-4o Image, Google Nano Banana Pro, Black Forest Labs FLUX). Supports text-to-image generation and image-to-image editing/transformation when SourceImage is provided. Configurable size, quality, style, and output format. Returns images as base64 or URLs.

Scheduled Geocoding: Maintenance action that finds records missing geocodes, retries failed geocoding attempts, and cleans up orphaned RecordGeoCode rows. Processes all pending records in parallel batches with cache invalidation. Designed to run on a schedule as a safety net for records that bypass BaseEntity.Save() (bulk SQL imports, direct DB operations).

Get Entity Details: Returns complete field information and sample data for a specific entity. Shows field names, types, descriptions, primary keys, related entities, and a few rows of actual data (3 by default, max 10, long values truncated). Perfect for understanding entity structure before writing SQL queries.

Get Entity List: Returns a lightweight list of all entities in the system with only name, schema, and description. Perfect for discovering available entities before exploring details. Uses cached metadata - extremely fast with no database queries.

File Storage: Get File Content: Smart file content retrieval with automatic extraction based on file type. Returns LLM-ready content: plain text for documents (PDF/Word/Excel extraction), base64 for images, decoded text for text formats. Optimized for AI agent consumption.

Google Custom Search: Performs web search using Google's Custom Search JSON API with advanced filtering and structured results. Provides high-quality search results with support for site filtering, date restrictions, file type filtering, and more.
Run Integration Sync: Triggers a data sync for a Company Integration. Pulls or pushes records according to entity maps, field maps, and watermarks configured for the integration.

Get Entity Schema For Form: Read-only action consumed by the Form Builder agent. Returns the curated form-relevant schema for an entity: field list with normalised types (string | number | boolean | datetime | enum | foreign-key), FK references resolved to {entity, displayField}, value-list fields annotated with allowedValues, and audit / virtual / computed fields stripped. The shape matches the CuratedFormSchema type in @memberjunction/interactive-component-types/forms.

documents.id: Action:Get Default Form Scaffold For Entity
documents.text: Get Default Form Scaffold For Entity: Read-only action that produces a working form-role ComponentSpec scaffolded from an entity's CodeGen metadata (Category, GeneratedFormSectionType, Sequence, FK relationships, value lists, EntitySetting icons). Mirrors the default Angular form layout. Agents call this first when authoring a net-new form, then modify the scaffold per user requirements — far fewer lint failures than writing JSX from scratch.

Get Active Form For Entity: Read-only action returning the currently-resolved interactive-form override (if any) for the (entity, requesting user) pair plus the full list of applicable variants. Returns null Active + empty Variants when no override exists. On an identity or permission entity (MJ: Users, Roles, Authorizations, API Keys and the like) only the caller's own User overrides apply, as on the form. Used by the Form Builder agent to decide between Create (no override exists) and Modify (an override already exists).

Create Interactive Form: Persists a net-new AI-authored or human-authored runtime form. Lints the supplied ComponentSpec (must declare componentRole='form'), inserts a Component row v1.0.0 with the spec, and creates an EntityFormOverride row that activates the form for the calling user. Returns ALREADY_EXISTS if the user already has an Active override for this entity — agents should call 'Modify Interactive Form' in that case. Scope is always clamped to 'User' regardless of any args — the action never writes Global or Role overrides.

Modify Interactive Form: Modify an existing interactive-form override. Routes off the source Override's status (not the underlying Component). Behavior is driven by the optional VersionBumpKind input: 'in-place' (default for Pending sources) overwrites the Pending Component row with no new version; 'patch'/'minor'/'major' snapshot a new Pending Component + sibling Override using the bumped version. Pending sources with a bump demote the prior Pending to Inactive (preserves rollback history). Active sources reject 'in-place' (would corrupt the live row) and default to 'minor'. Inactive sources reject 'in-place' (use Revert to re-activate first) but accept patch/minor/major as a branch-from-historical operation — default 'patch'; the Inactive source row is left untouched. Acts only on the caller's own User-scope overrides: a Role or Global override, or another user's, returns FORBIDDEN, because shared forms are managed from Form Builder or the form's Manage drawer. Any new override is User scope. The new Component and override (or, in place, the Component and the override's notes) are written in one transaction, so a refused override save leaves no Component change. Demoting the prior Pending source runs after that transaction; a failed demotion is logged and the new version stays.

Activate Interactive Form Version: Promote one of the caller's Pending EntityFormOverrides to Active; its Component and override flip in one transaction. Then, after that transaction, demotes the caller's other Active override on the entity to Inactive (and its Component); if that fails it returns PERSIST_FAILED with the target already Active. Activating an override that is already Active also sets aside the caller's other Active personal overrides for that entity (and their Components), so the target is the only Active personal one. The Pending Override is the one the agent just produced via Modify; activating it makes it the live form. Old Component rows persist forever as immutable history — revertible via 'Revert Interactive Form'. Acts only on the caller's own User-scope overrides: a Role or Global override, or another user's, returns FORBIDDEN, because shared forms are managed from Form Builder or the form's Manage drawer.

Revert Interactive Form: Re-point an Active EntityFormOverride at an older Component version in the same Name lineage. Pure UPDATE on the override row; no new Components or Overrides are created. Use to roll back to a prior working form when a recent change misbehaves. Old Component rows are never deleted, so revert is fully reversible by reverting again to the original version. Acts only on the caller's own User-scope overrides: a Role or Global override, or another user's, returns FORBIDDEN, because shared forms are managed from Form Builder or the form's Manage drawer.

List Storage Providers: Retrieves a list of active file storage providers configured in the system. Returns provider names, descriptions, and search support status. Useful for agents to discover available storage before searching or accessing files.

Materialize List From View: Create a new MJ List from a User View. Thin wrapper around ListOperations.MaterializeFromView. Captures lineage when RememberLineage=true. Cannot produce drops (target is new).
Add View Results To List: Append a User View's current results to an existing List. Always additive — never removes existing members. Dedupes silently.

Refresh List From Source: Refresh an existing lineage-bearing List against its captured source view (Additive or Sync mode). Sync-mode refreshes that would remove records require ConfirmDrops=true; otherwise rejected with DROP_NOT_CONFIRMED.

Compose Lists: Compose multiple List or View sources into a delta via a set-op (union / intersection / difference). Preview-only by default; supplying a Target projects the result into that list, which can trigger the drop-guard.
Share List: Grant a direct share on a List to a user or role. Idempotent at the (list, target) pair. Writes to ResourcePermission; emits a share-notification when sharing with a user.
Invite To List: Issue a pending-email invitation to share a List. Returns a generated token + expiry. Caller is expected to deliver an accept link to the recipient.
Unshare List: Revoke a previously-granted List permission. Soft-revokes (sets Status='Revoked' on ResourcePermission) so the audit trail remains intact.

Revoke List Invitation: Revoke a pending List invitation before it has been accepted. Returns INVITATION_ALREADY_USED if the invitation was already consumed — callers should use Unshare List against the resulting permission row in that case.

Resolve Audience: Resolve an AudienceSource (list / view / ad-hoc filter) to its current record IDs. Read-only — never mutates. Useful for previewing how many records a campaign would hit before sending.

Move List Members: Move (or copy) a set of records from one list to another. Move mode also removes the records from the source list — requires ConfirmDrops=true to actually delete. Copy mode skips the removal step.

Bulk Update List Item Status: Bulk-update the Status field on MJ: List Detail rows for a given list. NewStatus must match the MJ: List Detail Status check constraint (Active / Complete / Disabled / Error / Other / Pending / Rejected).

Send To Audience: Send a single message template to every record resolved from an AudienceSource. Wraps SendToAudience() in @memberjunction/communication-engine. Records missing the recipient field are skipped and surfaced in SkippedRecords output.

Test MCP Connection: Tests connectivity to an MCP server and retrieves server information including name, version, capabilities, and connection latency. Use this action to verify an MCP server is reachable and responding correctly before attempting to execute tools.

List MCP Tools: Retrieves the list of available tools from an MCP server connection. Returns tool names, descriptions, and input schemas for each tool. Use this action for discovery to understand what tools are available on a server before executing them.

Sync MCP Tools: Synchronizes tools from an MCP server to the local database. Discovers all available tools, adds new ones, updates existing tool definitions, and marks tools that are no longer available as deprecated. Use this action to keep the local tool catalog up to date with the server.

Execute MCP Tool: Executes a tool on an MCP server. Connects to the server if not already connected, calls the specified tool with provided arguments, and returns the result. This is the primary action for invoking external tool capabilities through MCP.
Clone Record: Clone a single entity record along with its configured child records and remapped relationships. Thin wrapper over RecordCloneEngine.

Clone Records: Clone several records of one entity, each with its configured child records and remapped relationships. Requires the 'Clone Records: Batch' authorization. Each root is cloned in its own transaction; ResultCode is PARTIAL when some succeed, and Results says which.

Run Record Process: Runs a MJ: Record Processes definition against a runtime scope (selected records, a view, a list, or a filter), optionally as a dry-run. Thin wrapper over the RecordProcessExecutor engine — the agent / workflow / low-code surface for the same bulk-update capability the Record Process Runner UX drives. For WorkType=FieldRules, a dry-run computes the exact per-record field diff without writing.

Read RSS Feed: Reads one or more RSS/Atom feeds and returns their articles, filtered by age and keywords. Every count that shaped the result is surfaced as an output param, so an empty answer is explainable without re-running.
Evaluate Record Against Rubric: Resolves the rubric to its latest Published version and evaluates the subject record. Returns the evaluation id, score, outcome, and per-criterion summary.
Get Rubric Consensus: Loads the subject's Submitted scores for the rubric and returns the consensus. The caller does not pass the scores.
Get Rubric: Returns the rubric tree for a name or id, or for a specific version. Does not score.

Create Rubric Draft: Stores a rubric tree as a Draft version. When RubricID is omitted and RubricName or Description is set, creates a new rubric first. Never publishes. Publishing stays a human action.
Get Rubric Subject: Loads the subject record for a rubric evaluation and returns the content the evaluator may read. Read-only. It does not score and it does not publish.
Submit Human Rubric: Stores a human evaluation and its scores, then marks it Submitted, in one transaction. Evidence is an evidence list. A percentage answer is a numeric value.

Run Ad-hoc Query: Executes a read-only SQL SELECT query for ad-hoc purposes with security validation. Supports {{query:"CategoryPath/QueryName"}} composition macros — the composition engine resolves these into CTEs before execution, enabling reuse of saved queries. Ensures SELECT-only operations, prevents dangerous SQL operations, enforces timeouts, and logs all queries for audit trail.

Run Cluster Analysis: Clusters an entity's embedding vectors (KMeans or DBSCAN), projects them to a 2D/3D layout via UMAP (PCA fallback), optionally names clusters with an LLM, and — when a PersistAs name is supplied — saves the result as an MJ: Cluster Analysis record. Thin wrapper over the framework-agnostic ClusteringEngine.

Run Decision: Answers typed questions about a state with a decision model, in one fast call: a Likelihood (the probability a statement is true), a Choice (one option from a described set) or a Score (a position on a rubric), each with probabilities. Use it for routing, gating and classification steps in agents and flows. It writes no text. Branch on a Choice or Score Value; treat probabilities as information until thresholds are calibrated.

Run Stored Query: Executes a stored query by ID or name, with optional parameters. Uses the full query pipeline including composition resolution, Nunjucks templating, caching, and audit logging. Preferred over ad-hoc SQL when a matching stored query exists.
Query Scheduled Jobs: Query scheduled jobs based on filter criteria including Status, JobTypeID, IsActive flag, and creation date ranges
Create Scheduled Job: Create a new scheduled job with the specified configuration including name, job type, cron expression, and optional parameters
Update Scheduled Job: Update an existing scheduled job. Only provided fields will be updated; omitted fields remain unchanged
Delete Scheduled Job: Delete an existing scheduled job from the system. Will fail if the job has related records that prevent deletion

Execute Scheduled Job Now: Run a scheduled job immediately, bypassing its cron schedule. Executes through the scheduling engine — lock acquisition, the job's plugin, the run record, statistics and notifications — and reports the job's actual outcome. Set Wait=false to start it and return without waiting.
Get Scheduled Job Statistics: Retrieve execution statistics for scheduled jobs including total runs, success/failure counts, success rate, and average duration

Scoped Search: Scope-aware universal search for AI agents. Enforces the calling agent's SearchScopeAccess ('All' | 'Assigned' | 'None') and resolves the requested scope against the agent's AIAgentSearchScope rows. Supports agent-invoked pre-rendered query templates, per-provider query transforms, multi-scope RRF fusion, and (optional) re-ranking. Returns ranked, scored, and enriched results in the same shape as the universal Search action.

Search Query Catalog: Searches the saved query catalog using vector-based semantic search. Takes a natural language description of what data is needed and returns ranked matching queries with similarity scores. Use this to find existing queries before writing ad-hoc SQL.

Search Storage Files: Searches for files across configured storage providers using native search APIs. Supports Google Drive, SharePoint, Dropbox, and Box with content search, file type filtering, date ranges, and path restrictions.

Search: Executes a universal search across the organization's knowledge base using vector similarity, full-text, and entity LIKE-based search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Returns ranked, scored, and enriched results. Designed for AI agents, MCP connectors, A2A connectors, and workflow orchestration.

Summarize Content: Creates a concise summary of content with citations to source material. Can work with either a URL (fetch + summarize) or pre-fetched content. Supports configurable summary length, optional citations with quotes and links, focus instructions for domain-specific summarization, and multiple output formats (paragraph, bullets, hybrid).

Create SVG Sketch Diagram: Creates hand-drawn/sketch-style SVG diagrams using Rough.js for informal, whiteboard-style visualizations. Supports flowcharts, org charts, and ER diagrams with configurable roughness and fill styles. Perfect for brainstorming presentations and informal documentation.
Tavily Search: Web search through the Tavily API, built for AI consumption: returns cleaned page content and an optional synthesised answer rather than only links.

Test Runtime Action: Runs a Runtime action against declared test cases. Accepts either (ActionID/ActionName) for an existing Action record or (Code + Configuration) for a freshly-generated, not-yet-persisted Runtime action. Each case runs through ActionEngine.RunAction so the full timeout / bridge / approval path is exercised. Returns per-case pass/fail plus AllPassed / PassedCount / FailedCount for the whole batch.
Validate Email Unique: Validates that an email address is not already in use by another user in the system
Assign User Roles: Assigns one or more roles to a user by creating UserRole associations. Accepts either a single role name (RoleName) or an array of role names (RoleNames).
Create User: Creates a new user in the MemberJunction system with validation and optional employee linking
Create Employee: Creates a new employee record in the MemberJunction system

Write Entity Field(s): Writes one or more fields onto a SINGLE entity record — either updating an existing record (identified by its PrimaryKey) or creating a new one (when CreateIfMissing=true and no PrimaryKey is supplied). A reusable write primitive for Flow Agents and as the terminal write-back step of a Feature Pipeline: give it the target entity, an optional primary key, and a field map, and it loads-or-creates, sets the fields, and saves. Respects entity validation, permissions, and audit trails (Record Changes). To always insert use Create Record; to read use Get Record / Run View.

Train ML Model: Trains a predictive model from an ML Training Pipeline definition. Carves a locked holdout, trains via the sidecar, persists an immutable Draft ML Model, and flags single-feature dominance (possible target leakage). Outputs the new model id, its honest holdout metrics, and whether it was leakage-flagged.

Score Record Set: Scores a set of records with a trained ML Model. The scope selects records (explicit ids / a saved view / a list / an entity+filter / a single record). Returns the scored count and either the ephemeral predictions or confirmation that scores were written back to the target.

Run Experiment Session: Executes an approved modeling plan as an experiment session — running its proposed experiments in waves to completion or until the budget bound, maintaining a leaderboard. Outputs the session id, the best (winning) model id, the final leaderboard, and why the session stopped.

Promote ML Model: Transitions an ML Model through its lifecycle (Validated / Published / Archived). Enforces the leakage sign-off gate — a model flagged for possible target leakage cannot be promoted unless SignOff=true. Lifecycle-only: never edits the model's metrics or artifact, only its Status.

Schedule Model Scoring: Binds a trained ML Model to write its prediction into a target entity column on a recurring schedule (e.g. monthly). Creates a scheduled Record Process that scores the rows selected by a filter and writes the prediction back into the chosen column on its cadence. Outputs the new Record Process id and the cron expression.

Calculate Array Statistics: Takes an array of numbers and returns summary statistics: count, min, max, sum, mean, median, stdDev, variance, and outliers detected via n-sigma distance from the mean. Pure compute — runs entirely inside the sandbox, no MJ metadata or entity access required. Useful as a building block for numeric summarization inside agent workflows, and as a smoke test for the Runtime Actions pipeline.

Entity Data Quality Report: Scans a sample of records for a given entity and returns a data quality report: per-field null rates, distinct value counts, and an overall completeness score (0-1) that weights non-nullable fields 2x. Useful for data stewards triaging bad data. Exercises the `md` (entity introspection) and `rv` (RunView) bridge namespaces.

Find Similar Records: Finds records in an entity whose text field is similar to a search string. Ranks matches by a blended score (30% containment, 70% normalized Levenshtein) so both typos and long-substring matches rank well. No AI dependency — cheap and deterministic. Validates the target field via metadata before scanning.

Summarize Entity Records: Queries a sample of records from the specified entity, passes them to an AI prompt, and returns a structured summary with key themes and suggested follow-up questions. Exercises the `rv` + `ai` bridge namespaces — the most common composition agents reach for.

Weekly Entity Digest: Composes a weekly markdown digest from activity across one or more entities, then emails it via the Send Single Message action. Exercises every major bridge namespace: metadata-bounded entity queries (rv), standard library helpers (libs), AI prompt rendering (ai), and downstream action invocation (actions). Supports dryRun=true to return the markdown without sending.

ActionSmith: Meta-agent that builds new Runtime actions for the MemberJunction action catalog. Defines the contract (inputs, outputs, minimal permissions, result codes, test cases), delegates code generation to Codesmith, runs tests via the sandbox, and persists the action for human approval. Ship capability gaps into the catalog without a developer in the loop.

Agent Manager: Top-level orchestrator agent responsible for creating, editing, and managing other AI agents in the MemberJunction system. Uses specialized sub-agents to gather requirements, design architecture, and craft prompts.

Demo Loop Agent: Simple demo agent showcasing loop agent capabilities. Can perform web searches, retrieve stock prices, get weather forecasts, look up census data, and fetch web page content. The AI dynamically determines the pathway and can execute multiple actions in parallel with no predetermined sequence.

Demo Minimal Loop Agent: Minimal prompt demo agent to showcase AgentTypePromptParams. Same capabilities as Demo Loop Agent but with most optional prompt sections disabled to demonstrate token savings.
Demo Flow Agent: Simple Agent Demo! This agent demonstrates the basic functionality of a flow agent, which follows a deterministic pathway
Marketing Agent: Strategic orchestrator for marketing content creation workflows, managing sub-agents to deliver high-quality marketing materials. Good at writing blog post.

Demo Harness Agent: Simple demo agent showcasing the Harness agent type. Its reasoning runs inside an external agent harness (Claude Code by default) with a sandboxed filesystem and shell, while MemberJunction keeps identity, permissions, governed data access, payload contracts, HITL and cost control. Ends each turn with the same next-step JSON envelope a Loop agent emits, so actions and sub-agents execute through MJ's existing validated machinery.

Betty: Dedicated knowledge base assistant agent that provides direct access to Betty Bot. Betty is trained on your organization's knowledge base and can answer questions about company policies, procedures, documentation, and institutional knowledge. This agent provides deterministic, single-step execution by forwarding queries directly to Betty and returning responses with optional reference links.

Codesmith Agent: Expert code generator and executor for data analysis and transformations. Generates JavaScript code, tests it in a secure sandbox, and iteratively refines it until successful. Supports lodash, date-fns, mathjs, papaparse, uuid, and validator libraries. Perfect for data manipulation, calculations, and analysis tasks.

Dashboards Expert: Builds and changes the Config dashboard open in the user's tab through browser tools: reads the layout, finds artifacts, views and queries, adds, removes, moves, resizes and configures panels, and asks the user to confirm saves and pins. Works in text chat and voice. Layout and composition only; it does not edit what is inside a component.

Database Designer: Conversational agent that guides users through creating and modifying MemberJunction database entities. Orchestrates Requirements Analyst, Schema Designer, Schema Validator, and Schema Builder sub-agents. Users describe what they want to store in plain English and Database Designer handles all the schema design and deployment.

Duplicate Resolution Agent: Agentic reasoning path for intelligent duplicate detection (the 'Agent' ReasoningMode on an Entity Document, for heavier entities that warrant deeper reasoning). Wraps the shared 'Duplicate Resolution' prompt so it can use memory notes and (Phase 2) context-exploration tools, while producing the same structured verdict (Merge/NotDuplicate/Uncertain + confidence + reasoning + survivor + field choices) as the cheap single-shot prompt path.

Infographic Agent: Specialized visualization expert that creates publication-quality SVG infographics from data and instructions. Composes multi-panel visualizations using charts, diagrams, networks, and word clouds. Can iterate to refine visualizations and intelligently assemble them into comprehensive infographics with professional layouts.

Knowledge Base Research Agent: Specialized agent for querying organizational knowledge bases and curated internal knowledge systems. Expert at conversational knowledge retrieval, policy interpretation, and connecting related organizational information. Handles tools like Betty and other knowledge management platforms to access company policies, procedures, documentation, and institutional knowledge.
Knowledge Agent: AI assistant specialized in knowledge management: semantic search, vectorization, duplicate detection, content navigation, and index configuration

Memory Cleanup Agent: System agent that archives stale notes and examples based on retention policies. Archives notes not accessed within NoteRetentionDays and low-scoring examples after ExampleRetentionDays. Runs on a daily schedule.

Memory Manager: System agent that automatically extracts notes and examples from conversations and agent runs. Analyzes user ratings and artifact usage to identify valuable learnings. Runs on a 15-minute schedule.

Model Development Agent: Conversational Loop orchestrator for Predictive Studio. Collaborates with a business user to build a strongly-typed ModelingPlanSpec via three specialist sub-agents (Goal Analyst, Data Scout, Experiment Designer), gates on explicit user approval, then drives the deterministic experiment session through the Run Experiment Session action (train/score/leaderboard/prune within budget), enforces the leakage warn/sign-off rule before any promotion, and authors an ML Experiment Results artifact with drill-through to the winning models. Mirrors the Agent Manager pattern: collaborate -> typed plan -> approve -> deterministic execution -> LLM report.

Query Builder: Business-friendly orchestrator agent that helps users explore their data and build saved queries. Delegates technical SQL work to the Query Strategist sub-agent. Presents results visually with diagrams and formatted tables, hiding SQL complexity unless the user asks for it.

Database Research Agent: Specialized sub-agent for conducting database research. Explores schema structure, formulates optimized SQL queries, executes research queries with security validation, and synthesizes findings from database analysis. Works as a component of the main Research Agent.

File Research Agent: Specialized agent for document and file system research. Expert at file type handling, content extraction strategies, document structure understanding, and cross-document synthesis. Handles storage provider enumeration, file search, and document analysis.

Web Research Agent: Specialized agent for internet and web-based research. Expert at search query formulation, source credibility evaluation, citation extraction, and content summarization. Handles Google search, web page retrieval, and content analysis.

Research Agent: Orchestrator agent for comprehensive research across multiple domains. Analyzes research requests, delegates tasks to specialized sub-agents (Web Research, Database Research, File Research, Report Writer), and coordinates the research workflow. Uses iterative methodology with source validation and contradiction detection. Delegates final synthesis and report generation to the Report Writer sub-agent.
Rubric Architect: Authors a rubric from a description or a numbered matrix, critiques the draft, and improves it from diagnostics and agreement. Writes Draft versions only and never publishes.
Rubric Evaluation Agent: Default agent for AgentRubricEvaluator. Scores one criterion at a time. It reads the rubric and the subject record. It does not publish and it does not create drafts.
Sage: Ambient agent in MJ that is always present in all conversations to help the user navigate functionality in MJ, handle basic requests, and bring in other agents to delegate work to

SkillSmith: Meta-agent that authors AI Skills for the skill catalog. Interviews the user about the capability, discovers bundle members with Find Candidate Actions/Agents, checks for overlapping existing skills, drafts agent-agnostic instructions with confirm-before-acting guardrails, gates on user approval, and persists the skill with its action and sub-agent junctions (default Status=Pending for human review).

User Onboarding Flow Agent: Automated flow agent for onboarding new users into MemberJunction. Handles permission verification, user creation, role assignment, and welcome email delivery through a deterministic workflow.

Realtime Co-Agent: Generic realtime companion. Acts as the live, low-latency front for any target MJ agent (the target is a runtime parameter) across realtime channels — voice today, plus interactive channels like the live whiteboard — holding a natural conversation while delegating real work back to that agent. Of the Realtime agent type; driven by a BaseRealtimeModel session rather than an iterative loop.

Schema Documentation Sweep: Finds MemberJunction entity fields that have no description and proposes one for each, then asks a person to approve them. A workflow demo that runs entirely on framework metadata — every install has undocumented fields, so it has real work to do on day one without any business data. The approval step is a genuine human-in-the-loop pause: the graph waits, every other branch keeps running, and answering releases it.

Content Pipeline: Researches a topic from two angles, drafts a short piece, and revises it against brand rules until it passes or gives up. A workflow demo of the two graph shapes a linear flow cannot express: a bounded While loop, and an exclusive pair where exactly one branch runs. The two research steps run in SEQUENCE, not in parallel — a Flow agent compiles with sequential traversal, where a step with two outgoing paths becomes an exclusive choice, so a fan-out would have meant 'either' and silently skipped one of them.

Default Decision: The decision prompt used when no other is named, by the Run Decision action and by loop agents. Its bindings choose the decision model. Callers normally pass the state explicitly, so the template only renders a state passed as template data.

Default Image Generation: The carrier prompt AIImageGenerationRunner uses when no other is named, including for the Generate Image action. Its bindings choose the image model and its failover settings apply; every call is recorded as an AI Prompt Run. The caller's prompt text goes straight to the image model, so the template only renders that text.

Default Rerank: The rerank prompt used when no other is named, by AIRerankerRunner and so by RerankerService.RerankNotes. It makes no chat call: its bindings choose the reranker model and its failover settings apply across them. Callers pass the query and documents directly, so the template only renders a query passed as template data.

Default Speech To Text: The carrier prompt AISpeechToTextRunner uses when no other is named. Its bindings choose the transcription model and its failover settings apply; every call is recorded as an AI Prompt Run. A transcript does not depend on the vendor, so failover may move to the next model (NextBestModel). The audio goes straight to the model and nothing in the template is rendered or sent.

Default Text To Speech: The carrier prompt AITextToSpeechRunner uses when no other is named. Its bindings choose the TTS model and its failover settings apply; every call is recorded as an AI Prompt Run. Voices belong to a vendor, so failover stays on the selected model's vendors (SameModelDifferentVendor) and never moves to a model whose voices differ; a caller whose voice matters pins the model. The caller's text goes straight to the speech model, so the template only renders that text.

Default Video Generation: The carrier prompt AIVideoRunner uses when no other is named. Its bindings choose the video model and its failover settings apply; every call is recorded as an AI Prompt Run. Avatars and assets belong to one provider account, so failover stays on the selected model's vendors (SameModelDifferentVendor). The request goes straight to the model and nothing in the template is rendered or sent.

Duplicate Resolution: Shared core reasoning instructions for intelligent duplicate detection. Given a source record + vector-surfaced candidate matches and their field deltas, decides Merge / NotDuplicate / Uncertain, strengthens or weakens the vector score, picks the surviving record and per-field survivor choices, and explains why. Used directly as the cheap single-shot 'Prompt' reasoning path AND wrapped by the Duplicate Resolution Agent for the 'Agent' path, so both modes share one instruction set.

Generate Remote Operation Code: Authors the TypeScript body of a Remote Operation's InternalExecute method from its Description + typed Input/Output contract, against the ambient input/provider/user/context. Used by MJRemoteOperationEntityServer for GenerationType=AI operations.

Query Builder - Query Strategist Prompt: System prompt for the Query Strategist sub-agent. Handles schema exploration, SQL generation, query testing, and structured result formatting.
Business Question Generator: Generates domain-specific business questions for entity groups
SQL Query Writer: Generates Nunjucks SQL query templates from business questions using few-shot learning
SQL Query Fixer: Fixes SQL syntax and logic errors in generated queries
Query Result Evaluator: Evaluates if a query correctly answers the business question
Query Refiner: Refines queries based on evaluation feedback
Entity Group Generator: Analyzes database schema to generate semantically meaningful entity groupings for business query generation

Realtime: Turn Moderator: Room turn moderator for multi-agent realtime voice meetings. Run once per turn (a fast prompt, NOT an agent run): given the room roster + recent diarized conversation, returns the ordered agent(s) who should speak next (0+). Routes direct address and relevance, lets productive agent-to-agent discussion continue, and goes quiet on unproductive ping-pong. Bound to GPT-OSS-120B on Cerebras for low latency; swap the model binding (e.g. to Gemma on Cerebras) without code changes.

Remote Browser Visual Interpreter: Fast vision prompt that lets a non-omnimodal realtime voice agent effectively SEE a live remote browser page. Given a viewport screenshot and a request, it returns a concise page description and/or localizes UI elements with pixel centroids (so the agent can browser_Click them). Backs the browser_DescribePage and browser_LocateElement tools.
Rerank Documents: LLM-based document reranking for semantic search. Scores and ranks documents by relevance to a query for two-stage retrieval systems.

Research Agent - Main Prompt: Main prompt for Research Agent that conducts comprehensive, iterative research by gathering information from multiple sources, comparing and validating data, and synthesizing findings into detailed reports.

Research Report Writer Prompt: Expert report writing and synthesis prompt for analyzing research findings and generating comprehensive reports with well-reasoned conclusions, confidence assessments, and proper citations.

Returning-Visitor Recap: Summarizes a support conversation into a short recap stored as an agent memory note, so a returning visitor's agent opens with prior context (returning-visitor memory, RV2). Plain-text output; emits NO_RECAP when there is nothing worth remembering.
Rubric Architect: System prompt for the Rubric Architect. It drafts, imports, critiques, and improves a rubric. It does not publish.
Rubric Evaluation Agent: System prompt for the Rubric Evaluation Agent. It scores one criterion at a time and does not publish.

Rubric Evaluator: The parent prompt of the LLM rubric evaluator. Renders the rubric's instructions, each criterion's rendered text (Criteria[].Text), the rules, and the reply contract the engine parses (SinglePass: decisions[]; PerCriterion: chosen + probabilities). The judge prompt renders into its judgePrompt slot. The subject is not in this template: it arrives as a separate, delimited user message. Swap it (SystemPromptID / SystemPromptName) only with a prompt that returns the same JSON. Template data: Rubric, Mode, Criteria, Subject; see the Rubrics Guide.

Rubric Criterion: Renders one rubric criterion as text: name, key, gate, description, guidance, hints, the evidence rule, the not-applicable rule, and its scale with each level's anchor. Rendered only, never sent to a model on its own. The LLM evaluator places the result in Criteria[].Text, and the Decision evaluator uses it as each Score question's instructions, so both describe a criterion the same way. Template data: Rubric, Criterion.

Rubric Evaluator - Default Judge: The judge the LLM rubric evaluator uses when the link names none: an impartial reviewer who scores only against the criteria and anchors, takes the lower of two levels, and does not reward length or tone.

Rubric Judge - Research Agent: A rubric judge written for Research Agent runs: what a good run of that agent looks like and the mistakes to score down. Rendered into the Rubric Evaluator prompt's judgePrompt slot when an agent-rubric link names it in EvaluatorConfig.PromptName.

Realtime Co-Agent - Progress Narration: One-off spoken-update instructions the Voice Co-Agent's realtime model receives while a delegated target-agent run is in flight. Contains a {{ progressMessage }} placeholder the client substitutes with the live progress message. Enforces strictly first-person narration (the co-agent owns the work): one short sentence, an explicit rewrite example, a ban on 'it'/the agent's name as the sentence subject, no repeated updates, and no generic filler. Resolved by name at session prepare time and threaded to the browser; clients fall back to built-in wording when this prompt is absent.

Realtime Co-Agent - System Prompt: System prompt for the Voice Co-Agent (Realtime agent type). Uses companion / 'voice for' framing so the model speaks on behalf of any target agent without impersonation. The target agent, its capabilities, the conversation so far, and the user's memory are injected at session start; the prompt is intentionally generic so one definition fronts any MJ agent.

Web Research Agent Prompt: System prompt for the Web Research Agent sub-agent. Guides the agent in formulating search queries, evaluating web sources, and extracting relevant research information from the internet.

Workflow Demo: Propose Field Description: Proposes a description for one undocumented MemberJunction entity field. Used as a Prompt step inside the Schema Documentation Sweep demo workflow, once per field.
Workflow Demo: Draft Content: Drafts a short piece from the research two prior steps gathered. Used as a Prompt step inside the Content Pipeline demo workflow, after the research join.

Workflow Demo: Brand Review: Reviews a draft against brand rules and returns the corrected version in the same pass, because a task graph is acyclic and cannot loop check-then-revise-then-check. The body of the While loop in the Content Pipeline demo workflow.

Workflow Demo: Final Note: Writes the closing note for the Content Pipeline demo workflow. Used by BOTH terminal steps of the exclusive pair — the approved branch and the gave-up branch — distinguished by a template parameter, so the two outcomes are one prompt with two truthful voices rather than two near-identical prompts.

Workflow Drafting: Turns a plain-English description of a repeatable process into a TaskGraphSpec — the steps and the dependencies between them — for the Create Workflow front door's "Describe it" entry. Returns a draft only; nothing is persisted until the author approves it on the canvas. Constrained to the agent names passed in, because a workflow referencing an agent that does not exist cannot be saved.
Workflow Planner - System Prompt: System prompt for the Workflow Planner sub-agent that designs and orchestrates multi-agent task graphs for complex requests.

Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite: Google's most cost-effective AI model, released March 3, 2026. Claude Sonnet 4.6: Anthropic's balanced performance model with enhanced long-context capabilities. 200K standard context window (1M in beta) with 64K output tokens. Claude Opus 4.7: Anthropic's flagship frontier model (April 2026). GPT 5.4-mini: OpenAI's cost-efficient mid-tier variant of the GPT 5.4 family, released March 17, 2026. Features 400K token context window and 128K output tokens. GPT 5.4-nano: OpenAI's smallest, cheapest member of the GPT 5.4 family, released March 17, 2026. Designed for classification, extraction, ranking, and sub-agent workloads. Grok 4.20: xAI's flagship frontier model (March 31, 2026). Features a 2M token context window and 128K output tokens. Aggressively priced at $2/$6 per 1M tokens vs Claude/GPT 5.4 flagships. Ships in reasoning and non-reasoning variants under the same pricing. Supersedes Grok 4 as xAI's top model.

Mistral Small 4: Mistral AI's unified multi-capability model (March 16, 2026), merging Magistral (reasoning), Pixtral (vision), and Devstral (agentic coding) into a single 119B-param MoE (6B active) under Apache 2.0. Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS: Google's expressive text-to-speech model (Preview, April 15, 2026). Qwen 3.6 35B A3B: Alibaba's open-weights Qwen 3.6 MoE model (April 15, 2026): 35B total parameters / 3B active. Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index of 43 — top-tier for open-weights; some multimodal metrics reach Claude Sonnet 4.5 level. RefCOCO 92.0 for visual grounding.

MiniMax-M2.7: MiniMax's frontier self-evolving MoE model (March 18, 2026). 228B total parameters in a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with native chain-of-thought reasoning (no separate thinking variant). 196K token context, 128K output capacity. Gemma 4 31B Instruct: Google's open-weights Gemma 4 31B instruction-tuned model released April 2, 2026. Mercury 2: Inception Labs' most powerful model, positioned as the fastest reasoning LLM. Grok 4.3: xAI's new flagship reasoning model, released April 30, 2026 (beta to SuperGrok Heavy on April 17). Always-on reasoning - 'thinks' before responding for every query. 1M token context window. Kimi K2.6: Moonshot AI's open-weight flagship coding and agent model, released April 20, 2026. 1-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts with 32B active parameters per token, native INT4 quantization, Modified MIT License (open weights on Hugging Face). 256K (262,144) token context window with output ceiling matching the context. Mistral Medium 3.5: Mistral AI's mid-tier model (May 1, 2026, public preview). 128B dense, open-weights under modified MIT license. 256K context. Qwen 3.6 Plus: Alibaba Cloud's flagship Plus-tier Qwen model released April 2, 2026. MoE architecture with always-on reasoning, 1M token context window, and 65K max output tokens. Qwen 3.6 Max Preview: Alibaba Cloud's top-tier flagship Qwen model released April 27, 2026. Proprietary, approximately 1T parameter MoE with 262K token context window. Scores #1 on six coding benchmarks. Highest capability tier in the Qwen 3.6 family. Available via Alibaba's DashScope API.

Qwen 3.6 Flash: Alibaba Cloud's cost-optimized Qwen model released April 27, 2026. 1M token context window, multimodal (text/image/video). Tiered pricing above 256K tokens. Drop-in successor to Qwen 3 Flash variants. Available via Alibaba's DashScope API.

Cohere Command A: Cohere's flagship language model released March 13, 2025. 111B parameter model with 256K token context window, optimized for RAG retrieval, agents, and tool-use. Strong multilingual support (23 languages). Premium tier in Cohere's Command family.

Cohere Embed v4: Cohere's flagship multimodal embedding model (text + image). 1536-dimensional default with Matryoshka representation learning (256/512/1024/1536 dim support). 128K token context. Dual pricing model: per-text-token and per-image-token. Replaces Embed v3 family for new workloads.

Gemini Embedding 2: Google's natively multimodal embedding model — maps text, images, video, audio, and PDF into one shared 3072-dimensional vector space (Matryoshka: truncatable down to 128 dims). 8,192 token input context; retrieval task instructions are carried in the text. GA April 2026.

Mercury Edit 2: Inception Labs' purpose-built diffusion LLM for next-edit prediction in IDEs and code editors. Released May 12, 2026. Same base pricing as Mercury 2 with significantly cheaper cached input. Optimized for very low-latency code-edit suggestion workflows where most prompt tokens are repeated context. OpenAI-compatible API.

Gemini 3.5 Flash: Google's cost-efficient frontier multimodal model released at Google I/O 2026 (May 19, 2026). Features 1M token input context window and 64K output capacity with configurable thinking levels (minimal/low/medium/high) for controlling the mix of quality, cost, and latency. Beats Gemini 3.1 Pro on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (76.2 vs 70.3), MCP Atlas (83.6 vs 78.2), Finance Agent v2 (57.9 vs 43.0), and GDPval-AA Elo (1656 vs 1314). 4x faster output tokens/sec than other frontier models. Qwen 3.7 Max: Alibaba Cloud's flagship Qwen 3.7 series 'Deep Thinking' (reasoning) model, made available via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (snapshot qwen3.7-max-2026-05-20) and announced at the 2026 Alibaba Cloud Summit. Structured Output, Batches, and Fine-tuning are not supported. Scores 57 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (#7 overall).

Qwen 3.8 Max: Alibaba Cloud's flagship Qwen 3.8 series reasoning model, generally available via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio on 2026-08-03 (API id qwen3.8-max). Successor to Qwen 3.7 Max. Open weights were announced for release on Hugging Face and ModelScope shortly after launch.

Claude Opus 4.8: Anthropic's frontier flagship released May 28, 2026, simultaneously available on Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.
