Grok Build 0.1: xAI's agentic coding specialist released May 29, 2026 as a functional successor to the retired Grok Code Fast 1. Features 256K token input context, no fixed output cap (up to 2M output tokens per response), always-on reasoning, tool calling, and structured outputs. Multimodal text+image input. Positioned as fast, low-cost coder for autonomous agent workflows.

Cohere Command A+: Cohere's first Mixture-of-Experts flagship released May 20, 2026. 218B sparse MoE under Apache 2.0 license with vision + text input across 48 languages. 128K input / 64K output context. Optimized for enterprise RAG, agents, and tool use. Successor to Cohere Command A.

MiniMax-M3: MiniMax's long-context multimodal flagship released June 1, 2026. Features the new MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) architecture for 9.7x faster prefill and 15.6x faster decode vs M2.7 at 1M context. 1M token context window. Native multimodal input (text + image + video) with desktop computer-use agent capabilities. Positioned as a long-context specialist complementing M2.7, not a replacement. Open weights and technical report promised within ~10 days of launch. OpenAI-compatible API.

Qwen 3.7 Plus: Alibaba Cloud's Plus-tier model in the Qwen 3.7 series, GA on Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Bailian) on 2026-06-01 at endpoint qwen3.7-plus. Multimodal (text, vision, video understanding) with deep-reasoning, tool invocation, and autonomous iteration capabilities. 1M token context window. Positioned as the cost-efficient sibling of Qwen 3.7 Max — roughly 1/6 the per-token price while preserving most of the agentic and reasoning capability of the Max tier. OpenAI-compatible API via DashScope; also surfaced on OpenRouter 2026-06-03.

Gemini 3.1 Flash Live: Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash Live model — its highest-quality native-audio realtime model (supersedes the deprecated 2.5 native-audio previews): streaming, full-duplex, tool-calling, for low-latency voice conversations over the Gemini Live API. Drives the Realtime agent type / Voice Co-Agent via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass GeminiRealtime).

ElevenLabs Agents: ElevenLabs Agents Platform — an orchestrated STT→LLM→TTS conversational stack treated as a realtime model: streaming, full-duplex, client-tool-calling voice sessions over the Agents websocket. The driver uses a MANAGED-AGENT strategy: the Model Vendor APIName is the managed agent's NAME (find-by-name, create-if-missing with the session tool set and per-session prompt-override enablement, PATCH on tool-set drift); deployments may instead set APIName to a concrete agent_… id to use a hand-configured agent verbatim. Drives the Realtime agent type / Voice Co-Agent via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass ElevenLabsRealtime).

AssemblyAI Voice Agent: AssemblyAI's Voice Agent API (launched April 2026) — a single-websocket speech-to-speech stack treated as a realtime model: Universal-3 Pro streaming ASR, server-side turn detection and barge-in, LLM reasoning, JSON-Schema tool calling, and conversational TTS (30+ voices, 6 languages). Per-session prompt/tool/voice/turn-detection config is supplied natively via session.update — no server-side agent object to manage. Flat $4.50/session-hour billing (no token usage events). Drives the Realtime agent type / Voice Co-Agent via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass AssemblyAIRealtime).

Grok Voice: xAI's Grok Voice Agent API — a streaming, full-duplex, tool-calling speech-to-speech realtime model. OpenAI-Realtime-API compatible (WebSocket endpoint wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime, Base64-encoded PCM16 @ 24 kHz audio), so the MJ driver reuses the OpenAI SDK pointed at xAI's base URL. Supports custom function tools plus xAI's built-in web search, X search, and RAG. Drives the Realtime agent type / Voice Co-Agent via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass GrokRealtime). Superseded by Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 (announced July 29, 2026); xAI's grok-voice-latest alias resolves to Think Fast 2.0 as of August 5, 2026, while this entry's pinned grok-voice API name continues to serve the prior generation.

Inworld Realtime: Inworld's Realtime API — a single-WebSocket, full-duplex, tool-calling speech-to-speech realtime stack. Input is streamed audio (server-side STT with voice profiling); output is synthesized speech via Realtime TTS-2 (supports inline steering tags like [laugh]). Inworld brokers many underlying LLMs selected per session via modelId (e.g. anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6); STT engine and TTS voice are configured independently. Turn-taking is semantic VAD with adjustable eagerness, handling true barge-in. Session components are swappable mid-session without reconnect via session.update. Supports fluent tool calling. Drives the Realtime agent type / Voice Co-Agent via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass InworldRealtime).

Kimi K2.7-Code: Moonshot AI's coding-specialist successor to Kimi K2.6, released June 12, 2026. 1-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts with 32B active parameters per token, Modified MIT License (open weights on Hugging Face). 256K (262,144) token context window. Purpose-built for software engineering: reports a +21.8 pp gain on Kimi Code Bench v2 over K2.6. Provides OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API at platform.moonshot.ai.

GLM 5.2: Z.AI's GLM 5.2 is an open-weights Mixture-of-Experts model with roughly 744-753B total parameters tuned for long-horizon autonomous coding and engineering tasks. Released to GLM Coding Plan tiers on June 13, 2026 with the standalone pay-per-token API live since June 16, 2026. 1M-token context window, MIT license, frontier-class coding performance reported to beat GPT-5.5 on multiple long-horizon coding benchmarks at roughly 1/6 the cost.

Nemotron 3 Ultra: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra is a 550B-total / 55B-active parameter hybrid Mamba-Transformer Mixture-of-Experts model built for frontier reasoning and orchestration in long-running agentic systems. Pre-trained in NVFP4 with Latent MoE and MTP layers. Released June 4, 2026 at Computex. 1M-token context. Open weights and training recipes available under the NVIDIA Open Model License (commercial use permitted). Distributed as an NIM microservice and across OpenRouter, Together AI, Anaconda, and build.nvidia.com.

Magistral Medium 1.2: Mistral AI's Magistral Medium is a native reasoning model that produces transparent chain-of-thought before its final answer. Version 1.2 (magistral-medium-2509) released September 18, 2025 with eight-language coverage (English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Arabic, Russian, Simplified Chinese) and a 128K context window. Magistral generates 2-5x more output tokens than generalist models because reasoning traces are verbose by design, so budget output spend accordingly.

Magistral Small 1.2: Mistral AI's Magistral Small 1.2 (magistral-small-2509) is the open-weights (Apache 2.0) counterpart to Magistral Medium, released September 18, 2025. Same transparent chain-of-thought reasoning, same eight-language coverage, same 128K context. Distributed via the Mistral API, Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter, and Hugging Face (mistralai/Magistral-Small-2509). Best fit for budget reasoning workloads.

Claude Sonnet 5: Anthropic's next-generation Sonnet-class flagship, released June 30, 2026 with simultaneous availability on Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. 1M-token context, 128K max output. Uses a new Claude 5 tokenizer that produces ~30-35% more tokens per input than Sonnet 4.6 — factor into per-request cost projections. Launch pricing $2/$10 per 1M tokens is in effect through August 31, 2026, after which standard pricing steps to $3/$15 per 1M (parity with Sonnet 4.6 per-token pricing). Supports streaming, JSON output, and adaptive effort levels. Positioned as a cost-neutral capability upgrade over Sonnet 4.6, closing much of the gap with Opus 4.8.

Claude Fable 5: Anthropic's Mythos-class Claude 5 flagship, made safe for general use through a safety-classifier layer that transparently declines or routes sensitive queries. Generally available on Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry starting June 9, 2026 (briefly withdrawn from AWS to comply with a US government export-control directive, restored on Amazon Bedrock on July 1, 2026 with stronger guardrails). 1M-token context, 128K max output. Pricing $10/$50 per 1M tokens is exactly 2x Opus 4.8's $5/$25 rate card. Companion Claude Mythos 5 shares the same specs and pricing without the safety-classifier layer, but is limited to Project Glasswing and trusted-access partners.

Nemotron 3 Super: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super is a 120B-total / 12B-active parameter hybrid Mamba-Attention Mixture-of-Experts model, released March 11, 2026 at GTC as the mid-tier of the Nemotron 3 family. Sits between Nemotron 3 Nano (30B) and Nemotron 3 Ultra (550B). 1M-token context. Open weights and training recipes available under the NVIDIA Open Model License (commercial use permitted). Distributed as an NIM microservice and across OpenRouter, Together AI, DeepInfra, and build.nvidia.com. A free-tier route is also available on OpenRouter at nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free.

Nemotron 3 Nano: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano is a 30B-total / 3B-active parameter hybrid Mamba-Attention Mixture-of-Experts model, released December 15, 2025 as the smallest and cheapest of the Nemotron 3 family. 262K-token context. Open weights and training recipes available under the NVIDIA Open Model License (commercial use permitted). Distributed as an NIM microservice and across OpenRouter and other inference providers. A free-tier route is also available on OpenRouter at nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b:free. Companion Nemotron 3 Nano Omni multimodal variant (vision/audio/language) available separately.

Qwen 3.6 27B: Alibaba's dense 27B-parameter flagship in the Qwen 3.6 open-weights family, released April 22, 2026 on Hugging Face and ModelScope. Native 262K-token context, extensible to 1M via YaRN scaling. Hybrid multimodal (text, image, video input; text output) with a built-in thinking mode. First open-source model to introduce Thinking Preservation, which retains chain-of-thought reasoning traces across multi-turn conversations. Available across Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (DashScope), OpenRouter, and Groq (preview at up to 486 tokens/sec). Strong repository-level code comprehension and front-end development performance.

GPT 5.6: OpenAI's flagship model, successor to GPT 5.5. Sets a new quality and efficiency baseline for complex production workflows. The gpt-5.6 API alias routes to the top-capability gpt-5.6-sol variant. Features a 1,050,000 token (~1M) context window and 128K output capacity. Supports adjustable reasoning via reasoning_effort (none, low, medium, high, xhigh, max) plus a new 'pro mode' that applies more model work before returning a single final answer. Adds Programmatic Tool Calling, multi-agent coordination, explicit prompt caching, and persisted reasoning. Knowledge cutoff February 2026.

GPT 5.6-terra: OpenAI's balanced GPT 5.6 variant that trades some capability for lower cost while retaining the full GPT 5.6 feature set. Features a 1,050,000 token (~1M) context window and 128K output capacity. Supports adjustable reasoning via reasoning_effort (none, low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Knowledge cutoff February 2026.

GPT 5.6-luna: OpenAI's efficient GPT 5.6 variant optimized for cost-sensitive, high-volume workloads. Features a 1,050,000 token (~1M) context window and 128K output capacity. Supports adjustable reasoning via reasoning_effort (none, low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Knowledge cutoff February 2026.

HuggingFace Speech-to-Speech: Hugging Face's open-source, self-hosted speech-to-speech stack treated as a realtime model: a cascaded VAD -> STT -> LLM -> TTS pipeline (Silero VAD, Parakeet/Whisper ASR, any OpenAI-compatible or local LLM, Qwen3-TTS/Kokoro/ChatTTS) exposing an OpenAI-Realtime-compatible /v1/realtime websocket. Private-by-design (audio never leaves owned infrastructure) and cost-free (no per-minute billing); component models are swappable. Reaches the browser through MJAPI's realtime proxy (client-direct topology) so the internal endpoint is never exposed and MJAPI stays the single ingress. Per-session prompt/tool/voice config is supplied natively via session.update; no server-side agent object and no token-usage events. Endpoint + optional auth are deployment config (HUGGINGFACE_REALTIME_URL / AI_VENDOR_API_KEY__HuggingFaceRealtime); set the key to a sentinel like 'none' for a keyless endpoint. DriverClass HuggingFaceRealtime. Low PowerRank so it is opt-in, not the default realtime provider.

Grok 4.5: xAI's flagship frontier reasoning model, released July 8, 2026. 500K token context window, native multimodal input (text, images, PDFs), tool calling, and structured output. Exposes reasoning_effort parameter (low / medium / high, default high). Priced aggressively at $2/$6 per 1M tokens with $0.50 cached-input, substantially undercutting Claude Opus 4.8 ($5/$25) while ranking as xAI's most capable model above Grok 4.20 and Grok 4.3.

GPT Realtime 2.1: OpenAI's speech-to-speech voice model released July 6, 2026 — the 2.1 update to GPT Realtime 2. Delivers GPT-5-class reasoning through the audio modality with five reasoning effort levels (minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh, default low), parallel tool/function calls, and a 128K token context (32K max output). Improves on GPT Realtime 2 with better alphanumeric recognition, silence/noise handling, and interruption/barge-in behavior, plus ~25% lower p95 latency from improved caching; pricing is unchanged from GPT Realtime 2. Multi-channel token pricing: $32/M audio input ($0.40 cached), $64/M audio output, $4/M text input ($0.40 cached), $24/M text output, $5/M image input ($0.50 cached). Streaming full-duplex realtime model driven via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass OpenAIRealtime). A smaller gpt-realtime-2.1-mini variant also exists.

GPT Realtime 2.1-mini: OpenAI's compact speech-to-speech voice model (gpt-realtime-2.1-mini), released July 6, 2026 alongside GPT Realtime 2.1. Brings the GPT Realtime 2.1 reasoning realtime stack — five reasoning effort levels (minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh, default low), parallel tool/function calls, 128K token context (32K max output), and audio/text/image input — to a cost-optimized tier for high-volume voice workloads. Multi-channel token pricing: $10/M audio input ($0.30 cached), $20/M audio output, $0.60/M text input ($0.06 cached), $2.40/M text output, $0.80/M image input ($0.08 cached). Streaming full-duplex realtime model driven via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass OpenAIRealtime).

Gemini 3.6 Flash: Google's token-efficiency refresh of the Flash line, released July 21, 2026. Built on Gemini 3.5 Flash (the model card defers architecture, training data, and safety policy to the 3.5 Flash card) and positioned as a cost-per-task improvement rather than a new capability tier: output price drops from $9.00 to $7.50 per 1M while emitting roughly 17% fewer output tokens. Features a 1M token input context window and 64K output capacity with configurable thinking. Leads its class on computer use (OSWorld-Verified 83.0), chart reasoning (CharXiv), and long-context recall (GDM-MRCR v2), but trails frontier coding models on SWE-Bench Pro and Terminal-bench 2.1. Supports multimodal input (text, image, video, audio, PDF) with text-only output, function calling, code execution, search grounding, and structured outputs. Live API and image/audio generation are NOT supported. Knowledge cutoff March 2026.

Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: Google's most cost-effective 3.5-generation model, released July 21, 2026 as a Stable (non-preview) model. Designed for high-volume, latency-sensitive workloads at $0.30/$2.50 per 1M tokens with a 1M token input context window and 64K output capacity. Supports configurable thinking levels for trading reasoning depth against cost. Scores 74.0 on OSWorld-Verified, unusually strong for a lite-tier model. Notably prices text, image, video AND audio input at a single unified rate - a departure from Gemini 2.5 Flash and 3.1 Flash-Lite, which charged an audio premium - and is flat-rate across the full 1M window with no context-length tiering. Supports function calling, structured outputs, and search grounding; audio generation, image generation, the Live API, and the dedicated Computer Use API surface are NOT supported. Knowledge cutoff March 2026.

Kimi K3: Moonshot AI's frontier-class open-weight multimodal MoE, released July 16, 2026. ~2.8T total parameters with sparse activation, 1M (1,048,576) token context, native multimodal input (text + images), and strong long-horizon coding and agentic capabilities. Modified MIT open weights on Hugging Face; direct API at platform.moonshot.ai (endpoint https://api.moonshot.ai/v1). Also listed as `moonshotai/kimi-k3` on OpenRouter. Pricing: $3.00 input / $15.00 output per 1M tokens with an aggressive $0.30 cached-input rate; flat across full context (no long-context surcharge). Positioned by Bloomberg and Simon Willison as closing the gap with U.S. frontier models. Direct successor to Kimi K2.6.

Inkling: Thinking Machines Lab's inaugural open-weights frontier model, released July 15, 2026. 975B total / 41B active mixture-of-experts transformer, multimodal pretraining on 45T tokens (text/image/audio/video), 1M token architectural context. NOTE: served context is provider-specific and lower than the architectural maximum — OpenRouter (Together-backed) serves 524,288 tokens, and Tinker offers 64K/256K options; the vendor rows carry the provider limits, not the 1M architectural figure. Apache 2.0 license with weights on Hugging Face at launch. Positioned by Artificial Analysis at release as the leading U.S. open-weights model. Accessible via Thinking Machines Lab's Tinker direct API (`inkling`, currently at 50% launch-promo pricing of $1.87/$4.68 per 1M) and via OpenRouter as `thinkingmachines/inkling` at $1.00 input / $4.05 output per 1M tokens. First major open-weights frontier release from a U.S. lab in 2026, from the team led by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati.

Claude Opus 5: Anthropic's fifth-generation Opus flagship, released July 24, 2026 with simultaneous availability on Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Same headline pricing ($5/$25 per 1M) as Opus 4.8 with a doubling of Frontier-Bench v0.1 performance versus Opus 4.8; comes within 0.5% of Fable 5 on CursorBench 3.2 at half the cost and surpasses Fable 5 on OSWorld 2.0 at one-third the cost. Features 1M-token context, 128K max output (300K via `output-300k-2026-03-24` batch beta), adaptive thinking with `effort` defaulting to `high` on the API and Claude Code, mid-conversation tool changes (beta), automatic safety fallbacks (beta), visual output generation, and stronger agentic self-verification. Fast mode available at ~2.5x speed for 2x cost ($10/$50 per 1M). Knowledge cutoff May 2026. Also available on OpenRouter as `anthropic/claude-opus-5` with `anthropic/claude-opus-5-fast` as the fast-mode variant. Direct successor to Claude Opus 4.8.

Kimi K3 Fast: Fireworks.ai's Fast-tier serving path for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 — identical weights and capabilities to standard Kimi K3, served on a dedicated high-throughput endpoint at roughly 2x the generated-token speed (~200 tps vs ~100 tps Standard) for roughly 1.5x the price. Invoked through a distinct router model ID (`accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k3-fast`), not a per-request flag, which is why it is modeled as its own entry rather than a second vendor row on Kimi K3. 1M-token context, 131,072 max output, function calling supported. Use for latency-sensitive agentic loops where iteration speed dominates token cost; use standard Kimi K3 for batch and throughput-insensitive work. Fast tier has no Priority variant.

Claude Opus 5 Fast: Anthropic's Fast-mode variant of Claude Opus 5 — identical weights, capabilities, and 1M-token context, served at approximately 2.5x output throughput for 2x the price ($10/$50 per 1M vs $5/$25). The premium buys latency, not intelligence. DEPRECATED AS AN API MODEL ID (2026-09-01): Anthropic retired the dedicated `claude-opus-5-fast` model id (and `claude-opus-4-8-fast`) in favour of requesting fast mode on the base model — `claude-opus-5` with `speed: "fast"` (or `service_tier: "fast"`) and the `fast-mode-2026-02-01` beta header. Anthropic's fast-mode documentation now lists only `claude-opus-5` and `claude-opus-4-8` as supported models. Existing requests to the dedicated id keep working and are served by the same fast-tier capacity, so this record's Anthropic route is marked Deprecated rather than Inactive and its cost row stays Active — but new integrations should target the base model. MJ has no schema field for a per-request speed tier, so how (or whether) to express fast mode once the dedicated id is withdrawn is an open modelling decision; see the 2026-09-21 research report. OTHER AVAILABILITY LIMITS: fast mode is a research preview on the Anthropic first-party API only (access is account-managed / waitlisted) — it is NOT available on Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Vertex AI, or Microsoft Foundry, and is NOT supported by the Batch API or Priority Tier. Also routable via OpenRouter as `anthropic/claude-opus-5-fast`, whose listing carries the same deprecation notice. Use standard Claude Opus 5 for batch workloads and any cloud-hosted deployment.

Qwen 3.7 Flash: Alibaba Cloud's Flash-tier model in the Qwen 3.7 series, released 2026-07-27 at endpoint qwen3.7-flash. A vision-language reasoning model built for multimodal agents, visual coding, search, and computer/UI interaction, with claimed strengths in object recognition and spatial understanding. 1M token context window, 65,536 max output tokens. Positioned as the low-cost speed tier of the 3.7 family at $0.03/$0.13 per 1M tokens — roughly an order of magnitude cheaper than Qwen 3.7 Plus while retaining the series' vision and reasoning capability. OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API via DashScope; also listed on OpenRouter as qwen/qwen3.7-flash on 2026-07-29. Direct successor to Qwen 3.6 Flash.

Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0: xAI's second-generation speech-to-speech realtime voice model, announced July 29, 2026; the grok-voice-latest alias resolves to it as of August 5, 2026. Reasons while speaking rather than pausing to think — ~60% fewer reasoning tokens than Think Fast 1.0 at ~0.70s time-to-first-audio. Transcription WER 1.5-2.0x better than dedicated STT (Deepgram Nova 3, ElevenLabs Scribe v2) on xAI's 24-language eval, widening to ~10x in noisy environments; 20+ languages with automatic language detection. OpenAI-Realtime-API compatible (WebSocket endpoint wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime), so the MJ driver reuses the OpenAI SDK pointed at xAI's base URL. Supports custom function tools plus xAI's built-in web search, X search, collections search, and remote MCP tools. Priced per minute of audio ($0.08/min API list price). Drives the Realtime agent type / Voice Co-Agent via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass GrokRealtime).
Whisper Large v3: OpenAI's Whisper Large v3 speech recognition model. Multilingual transcription across 90+ languages with strong accuracy on accented speech, background noise and domain vocabulary.
Whisper Large v3 Turbo: A distilled, substantially faster variant of Whisper Large v3, trading a small amount of accuracy for a large reduction in transcription time and cost.

Whisper 1: OpenAI's hosted Whisper transcription endpoint. Serves the Whisper large-v2 checkpoint rather than v3, so it is a distinct model from Whisper Large v3 despite the shared lineage. Multilingual transcription across 90+ languages.

Inkling Small: Thinking Machines Lab's distilled open-weights sibling to Inkling, released July 30, 2026 with full Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face. 276B total / 12B active mixture-of-experts, multimodal (text + image + audio), variable thinking effort, and a context window up to 1M tokens architecturally. NOTE: served context is provider-specific — OpenRouter (`thinkingmachines/inkling-small`) currently serves 524,288 input tokens with a 262,144 max output. Thinking Machines Lab's own tables show Small ahead of full Inkling on Humanity's Last Exam (text-only) and SWE-bench Verified while trailing on SimpleQA — a distillation trade-off, not a strict subset of capability. Direct Tinker API meters prefill/sampled/training/cached-prefill tokens rather than input/output (promotional launch rates $0.58/$1.44/$1.73/$0.116 per 1M), which does not map cleanly onto MJ's per-1M-input/output cost schema — the cost row here uses the OpenRouter route ($0.45/$1.20 per 1M) instead, matching how the base Inkling entry handled the same asymmetry.

Grok 4.6: xAI's frontier reasoning model, released August 12, 2026 as the next evolution of Grok 4.5. Positioned by xAI for long-running agents, coding, knowledge work, research, and ambitious interactive or visual work. 500K token context window with native text + image input, low/medium/high/xhigh reasoning_effort, and tool calling. Same headline $2/$6 per 1M price point as Grok 4.5 for prompts below 200K tokens, with a tiered long-context rate of $4/$12 above 200K (both cached input rates double correspondingly). Available via xAI direct API, Grok Build, OpenRouter, and partners including Cursor, Vercel, and Cloudflare. Launch promo (through the first week): 2x included usage inside Grok Build and Cursor.

Gemini 3.7 Flash: Google's next-generation Flash-tier model, released August 13, 2026. Successor to Gemini 3.6 Flash (July 21, 2026) positioned by Google as a cost-per-task improvement targeting coding and agentic workloads, shipped with a 50% introductory price cut versus its predecessor's headline rate. 1M token input context / 65K output cap. Multimodal input (text, image, video, audio, PDF); text output. Supports function calling, code execution, search grounding, structured output, and configurable thinking (reasoning effort). Introductory pricing $0.75/$3.75 per 1M input/output tokens runs through December 31, 2026; standard pricing steps up to $1.50/$7.50 on January 1, 2027 (parity with Gemini 3.6 Flash's headline rate). Cached input $0.075/1M during intro period.

GLM 5.3: Z.AI (Zhipu AI) flagship LLM released 2026-08-14, successor to GLM-5.2. 743B base parameters. Reported leader on CyberGym and AutomationBench evaluations at launch. Open weights staged behind safety review at launch time. Z.AI posted the per-token rate card effective 2026-08-19 ($1.40 input / $4.40 output / $0.26 cached input per 1M), recorded below; the model also remains available through the GLM Coding Plan ($18/mo starting) and Z.AI's ZCode agent. Sources: https://emergent.sh/news/glm-53-officially-launched ; https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.3 ; https://models.dev/models/zhipuai/glm-5.3/ ; https://www.explainx.ai/blog/glm-5-3-launch-cyber-defense-benchmarks-august-2026

GLM-5.3-Flash: Z.AI (Zhipu AI) cost-tier Flash companion to GLM-5.3, released 2026-08-26 with MIT-licensed open weights. Native multimodal (text/image/video/agentic), 320B total / 18B active parameters (MoE), 1.3M token input context and 131,072 token max output. Reportedly hit #1 on the OpenRouter usage leaderboard shortly after launch. Previously surfaced as the 'Ox Alpha' stealth preview on OpenRouter (posted Aug 20) before being de-anonymised as GLM-5.3-Flash on Aug 26. Sources: https://openrouter.ai/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash ; https://www.orcarouter.ai/blog/glm-5-3-flash-release ; https://kie.ai/blog/what-is-glm-5-5 ; https://www.explainx.ai/blog/ox-alpha-what-we-know-mystery-ai-model-august-2026

Qwen3.8-Flash: Alibaba Cloud (Qwen) cost-tier Flash companion to Qwen 3.8 Max, released 2026-08-26. 125B parameters, multimodal reasoning across text / image / video / agentic surfaces, 1,000,000-token input context and 131,072-token max output. Positioned by Alibaba as a low-cost general-purpose reasoning model. Sources: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-26/alibaba-releases-smaller-cost-effective-qwen-ai-model ; https://mpost.io/alibaba-prices-qwen3-8-flash-api-at-0-16-per-million-tokens-cutting-inference-costs-for-125b-parameter-model/ ; https://openrouter.ai/qwen/qwen3.8-flash

Claude Fable 5.1: Anthropic's Mythos-class Claude 5 flagship, released September 1, 2026 as the successor to Claude Fable 5. Generally available on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry. 1M-token context, 128K max output, adaptive thinking always on with a five-level effort setting (defaults to high). Per-token price is unchanged from Fable 5 at $10/$50 per 1M; the change is prompt caching - cache hits and refreshes drop 75% from $1 to $0.25 per 1M (0.025x base input, versus the standard 0.1x multiplier used by every other Claude model). 5-minute cache writes $12.50/1M, 1-hour writes $20/1M. Anthropic estimates ~25% savings on typical workloads and up to ~45% on heavily agentic ones. Uses the Claude 4.7-and-later tokenizer (~30% more tokens for the same text than Sonnet 4.6 and earlier). Companion Claude Mythos 5.1 shares the same specs and rate card but is limited-availability through Anthropic's Cyber Verification and Life Sciences Verification programs (Project Glasswing) and is therefore NOT modelled here. Tentative retirement not sooner than September 1, 2027.

GPT-6 Astra: OpenAI's GPT-6 generation flagship, released September 3, 2026 as the successor to the GPT 5.6 family. 1,050,000-token (~1M) context window with a 128K output cap. Positioned for long-horizon agentic work; supports streaming, Structured Outputs, computer use, Programmatic Tool Calling, multi-agent orchestration, explicit prompt caching and persisted reasoning. reasoning.effort accepts low, medium, high, xhigh and max - unlike GPT 5.6 it does NOT accept none. LONG-CONTEXT SURCHARGE: a request whose input exceeds 272,000 tokens is rebilled in its entirety at 2x input/cache and 1.5x output ($20 input, $2 cached input, $25 cache write, $75 output per 1M). The cost record below carries the short-context (<=272K) rate only. Astra is the first OpenAI model to reach the Critical cyber-capability threshold under the Preparedness Framework, so advanced cyber capability is gated behind the separate Daybreak program and is not part of the ordinary API surface. Rollout began with a limited set of organizations on September 3 and widened across ChatGPT, Codex and the API over the following days.

Gemini 3.8 Flash: Google's Flash-tier model released September 2, 2026 as the successor to Gemini 3.7 Flash (August 13, 2026), targeting coding agents and enterprise agentic workloads. 1M-token input context / 64K output cap. Multimodal input (text, image, audio, video, PDF); text output. Supports function calling, code execution, search grounding, structured output and tunable thinking levels (low, medium, high). Knowledge cutoff March 2026. Introductory pricing $0.75/$3.75 per 1M input/output holds Gemini 3.7 Flash's headline rate and runs through December 31, 2026; standard pricing steps up to $1.50/$7.50 on January 1, 2027, when context caching also doubles from $0.075 to $0.15 per 1M and cache storage from $0.50 to $1.00 per 1M per hour.

Muse Spark 1.3: Meta's most capable model, released September 2, 2026 - a multimodal reasoning system built for long-horizon agentic work, coding and computer use. Accepts text, image and video input; 1,048,576-token context window. Supports function calling and structured (JSON) output. Meta reports ~20% fewer tool calls and ~25% fewer tokens than Muse Spark 1.2 on comparable coding tasks. Meta has published neither a parameter count nor a maximum output length, and the model's max reasoning mode is held back pending further safety testing, so MaxOutputTokens is deliberately left unset here. Standard tier is $1.25/$4.25 per 1M with $0.15/1M cached input. A separate Contributor tier runs $0.10/$0.20 per 1M in exchange for allowing Meta to train on submitted prompts and outputs - that tier is NOT modelled here because it carries a data-use commitment that is a policy decision, not a pricing one. Reached here through OpenRouter (meta/muse-spark-1.3); Meta's own first-party API is not wired up because MJ has no Meta driver class yet.

GPT-Live 1: OpenAI's GPT-Live 1 speech-to-speech realtime model. Features native full-duplex conversational audio with dual delegation (local and remote reasoning planes) over raw WebSocket and SIP, supporting PCM16, G.711 μ-law, and A-law formats with per-minute billing ($0.05/min).

Fugu Max: Sakana AI's cost-performance orchestration model, released September 11, 2026. Fugu is not a single model but a learned multi-agent orchestrator: a language model trained to route each task across a fixed pool of open-weight and specialist models (including NVIDIA's Nemotron family) and to recursively call instances of itself, then stitch the results together. Fugu Max dynamically selects efficient combinations of expert agents to improve quality and cost together. 1,048,576-token context window, 128,000-token maximum output, priced flat regardless of context length. Accepts text, image and PDF input and returns text. Supports function calling, structured (JSON) outputs via response_format, configurable reasoning effort (high, xhigh, max), and built-in web search and web fetch (billed separately at $10 per 1,000 search calls, which MJ does not model). Reached here through OpenRouter (sakana/fugu-max); Sakana's own OpenAI-compatible API is not wired up because MJ has no Sakana driver class yet. Note: Sakana does not serve the Fugu family inside the EU or EEA pending GDPR compliance work.

Fugu Ultra v2: Sakana AI's highest-capability orchestration model, released September 11, 2026, successor to Fugu Ultra. Like the rest of the Fugu family it is a learned multi-agent orchestrator rather than a single model: it routes each task across a pool of open-weight and specialist models and recursively calls instances of itself. Fugu Ultra v2 prioritises answer quality on complex multi-step reasoning, autonomous research and full-stack software development, and notably does not rely on any proprietary frontier model in its pool. 1,000,000-token context window, 128,000-token maximum output. Accepts text, image and PDF input and returns text. Supports function calling, structured (JSON) outputs, configurable reasoning effort (high, xhigh, max) and built-in web search. Reached here through OpenRouter (sakana/fugu-ultra-v2); Sakana's own OpenAI-compatible API is not wired up because MJ has no Sakana driver class yet. Note: Sakana does not serve the Fugu family inside the EU or EEA pending GDPR compliance work. Ranks are set conservatively - Sakana's benchmark claims are strong but the orchestration architecture means latency and per-task token consumption are both higher than a single-model call of comparable quality.

Gemini 3.8 Live: Google's Gemini 3.8 Live multimodal realtime model for low-latency streaming voice, audio, and visual interaction over the Gemini Live API. Features native full-duplex conversational audio, visual frame input up to 1 fps, and non-blocking and blocking tool calling. Drives the Realtime agent type / Voice Co-Agent via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass GeminiRealtime).

Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking: Google's Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking model with asynchronous reasoning, thought summaries, and non-blocking tool execution for complex real-time problem solving. Uses interactionStatus (IN_PROGRESS/IDLE) for turn management and supports thinkingLevels low/medium/high. Drives the Realtime agent type / Voice Co-Agent via BaseRealtimeModel (DriverClass GeminiRealtime).

GLM-5.3-FlashX: Z.AI (Zhipu AI) high-speed serving variant of GLM-5.3-Flash, released 2026-09-18. Same capability base as GLM-5.3-Flash — native multimodal (text/image/video/agentic), 320B total / 18B active parameters on a hybrid sparse + linear attention MoE, 1M-token context and 131,072 max output — served at up to 200 tokens/s for roughly 2.5x the per-token price ($0.37/$1.25 against Flash's $0.15/$0.50). FlashX is a serving and inference upgrade, not a separately documented intelligence checkpoint, so PowerRank matches GLM-5.3-Flash and only CostRank moves. Targeted at visual coding, tool use and long-horizon agent workloads that are latency-bound rather than quality-bound. Note that Z.AI added GLM-5.3-Flash to its GLM Coding Plan subscription but left FlashX off it, so FlashX is metered API only. Sources: https://openrouter.ai/z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx ; https://docs.z.ai/guides/vlm/glm-5.3-flash ; https://www.cometapi.com/what-is-glm-5-3-flashx/ ; https://www.orcarouter.ai/blog/glm-5-3-flashx-release ; https://apimaster.ai/blog/glm-5-3-flashx-api

Claude Opus 5.5: Anthropic's Opus-class flagship, released September 22, 2026 as the successor to Claude Opus 5 and now Anthropic's recommended default for most workloads. Built for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work; Anthropic positions it as matching Claude Fable 5.1 on most tasks at lower cost and lower latency. 1M-token context included at standard pricing, 128K max output (300K on the Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header), adaptive thinking always on with an effort setting that defaults to medium (versus high on Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5). Supports structured outputs (JSON schema via response_format), strict tool use, streaming and vision. Per-token price is $4/$20 per 1M - 20% below the $5/$25 shared by Opus 5, 4.8, 4.7, 4.6 and 4.5 - and cache hits are $0.20/1M, a 0.05x base-input multiplier that sits between Fable 5.1's 0.025x and the standard 0.1x. Anthropic reports ~40% lower cost on typical workloads, attributing part of that to fewer tokens and fewer turns rather than the rate alone. Uses the Claude 4.7-and-later tokenizer (~30% more tokens for the same text than Sonnet 4.6 and earlier). Available on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock (anthropic.claude-opus-5-5), Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry (both claude-opus-5-5); only the Claude API, Bedrock and OpenRouter routes are modelled here. Fast mode (research preview, Claude API only) serves this model at a $8/$40 premium and is not modelled as a separate record. Tentative retirement not sooner than September 22, 2027.

Grok 4.7: xAI's frontier reasoning model, released September 21, 2026 as the successor to Grok 4.6 and xAI's recommended model for coding, agents and general text work. Built on a new and larger base model than 4.6, trained with a longer reinforcement-learning run on a harder task mixture weighted toward problems that take many hours. Independent measurement shows a broad gain over 4.6 rather than a narrow one: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index 56 vs 47 (DeepSWE v1.1 73% vs 65%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 33% vs 18%, SWE-Atlas-QnA 63% vs 58%), GDPval-AA 1695 Elo vs 1605, analytical quality 1994 Elo vs 1690, and a lower AA-Omniscience hallucination rate (29% vs 34%). 500K-token context window retained from 4.6, native text + image input with text-only output, low/medium/high/xhigh reasoning effort (high is the documented default), tool calling, May 2026 knowledge cutoff. Price is unchanged from 4.6: $2/$6 per 1M below 200K prompt tokens, with the whole request re-rated at $4/$12 (cached input $0.50 -> $1.00) once a prompt reaches 200K. Available via xAI direct, OpenRouter and GitHub Copilot; Amazon Bedrock and Azure/Microsoft Foundry still list 4.6 as their newest Grok and are deliberately NOT wired here yet. NOTE on MaxOutputTokens: xAI publishes no text output cap for this model, and the 450,000-token figure circulating on third-party model cards is unofficial and conflicts with xAI's own 'no stated limit' wording - 128000 is carried over from the Grok 4.6 route as a deliberately conservative floor and should be raised once xAI documents a real number.

GPT-6 Sol: OpenAI's mid-tier GPT-6 model, released September 22, 2026 nineteen days after flagship GPT-6 Astra and roughly 90 minutes after Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5.5. Positioned as the cheaper, faster sibling to Astra for complex coding, professional knowledge work and computer use. 1,050,000-token context, 128K max output, selectable reasoning effort, streaming, structured outputs. Priced at $2/$10 per 1M - half the $4/$20 that the GPT-5.6 generation settled at - which places it in the same rate band as Claude Opus 5.5. Benchmarks are genuinely mixed rather than uniformly better: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index 57 at max effort (up 2 from GPT-5.6 Sol, with Terminal-Bench 4.0 43% vs 37% and SWE-Atlas-QnA 58 vs 54), but DeepSWE (68.8%) and OSWorld 2.0 (64.4%) both land BELOW GPT-5.6 Sol's best (72.7%, 66.2%) and below Claude Opus 5's best (73.7%, 70.2%), and Claude Opus 5.5 leads it by roughly 7 points on AutomationBench and 5 on FrontierCode. Available on the OpenAI API, Microsoft Foundry / Azure OpenAI (Standard across all 28 global regions plus US and EU data zones, with Provisioned Throughput and Priority Processing), Amazon Bedrock (US and global, plus Bedrock Mantle) and OpenRouter. No PriorVersionID is set: its natural predecessor is gpt-5.6-sol, which MJ does not carry, and GPT-6 Astra already claims GPT 5.6.

GPT-6 Luna: The cheapest rung of OpenAI's GPT-6 ladder, released September 22, 2026 alongside GPT-6 Sol. Aimed at focused, high-volume work - classification, extraction, routing, short-turn assistants - rather than long-horizon agentic tasks. 1,050,000-token context, 128K max output, selectable reasoning effort, streaming, structured outputs. Priced at $0.10/$0.50 per 1M, half the $0.20/$1.20 that GPT-5.6-luna settled at, which makes it one of the cheapest frontier-lab routes available. Quality per dollar is the headline: it scores 37.26 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index against Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite's 22.17 while costing 3x less on input and 5x less on output, and it declines to answer only 23.3% of the questions it does not know versus Flash-Lite's 65.6%. It loses to Flash-Lite on multimodal reasoning (MMMU-Pro 75.5% vs 79.0%). A full Intelligence Index run costs about $0.07 per task at max effort, roughly 60% less than GPT-5.6-luna at the same setting. Available on the OpenAI API, Microsoft Foundry / Azure OpenAI (Standard across all 28 global regions plus US and EU data zones), Amazon Bedrock (US and global, plus Bedrock Mantle) and OpenRouter. NOTE: 'gpt-6-luna-pro' is NOT a separate model - it is this model served with reasoning.mode set to pro, and is deliberately not recorded as its own record for the same reason Claude fast mode is not.

MiMo V2.6 Pro: Xiaomi's flagship open-weight foundation model, released September 22, 2026 and open-sourced under the MIT licence along with the rest of the MiMo V2.6 family. Mixture-of-Experts at over 1T total parameters, natively omnimodal (text, image, video and audio input; text output), 1,050,000-token context, 131K max output, function calling and JSON-schema structured outputs. Reported to top the open-weight field on release; the reinforcement-learning run behind it took under six days and about $2.62M of compute. Listed at $0.435/$0.87 per 1M on Xiaomi's own API and at the same rate on OpenRouter. MJ reaches this model through OpenRouter only: no Xiaomi driver class exists, so the Xiaomi vendor row records attribution as Model Developer and carries no inference route. NOTE: InheritTypeModalities is true, so this record inherits the LLM type's modalities and therefore does NOT express the video and audio input this model actually accepts - explicit MJ: AI Model Modalities rows would be needed for that and are not authored here. A MiMo-V2.6-Pro-UltraSpeed serving variant also exists and is not modelled.

MiMo V2.6 Flash: The fast, inexpensive member of Xiaomi's MiMo V2.6 family, released September 22, 2026 under the MIT licence. Mixture-of-Experts with 309B total parameters and 15B activated per token using hybrid attention, natively omnimodal (text, image, video and audio input; text output), 1M-token context, 128K max output, function calling and JSON-schema structured outputs. Its reinforcement-learning run cost about $0.85M against $2.62M for MiMo V2.6 Pro. Listed at $0.14/$0.28 per 1M, roughly a third of Pro's rate. MJ reaches this model through OpenRouter only: no Xiaomi driver class exists, so the Xiaomi vendor row records attribution as Model Developer and carries no inference route. NOTE: InheritTypeModalities is true, so this record inherits the LLM type's modalities and therefore does NOT express the video and audio input this model actually accepts.

Betty: The MJ-native, organization-scoped assistant, reached through the Betty Public API v1. Answers are grounded in the organization's own content and come back with citations, which the driver surfaces as additional choices. Distinct from the Betty Bot model, which is a different service on a different wire protocol.

Eleven v4: ElevenLabs' flagship v4 text-to-speech model, announced September 2026. Successor to Eleven v3, with broader language coverage and richer audio-tag control over delivery and emotion. Called through the ElevenLabs API as model_id eleven_v4.

Eleven v4 Turbo: Low-latency variant of ElevenLabs' v4 text-to-speech model, announced September 2026 and built for real-time, conversational use. Called through the ElevenLabs API as model_id eleven_v4_turbo.

Claude Sonnet 5.5: Anthropic's Sonnet-class model, released September 28, 2026 as the successor to Claude Sonnet 5, and the named replacement for claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (retiring 2026-11-30). 1M-token context, 128K max output (300K on the Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header). Adaptive thinking with an effort setting that defaults to high; the between_tools option turns off up-front thinking. Non-default temperature, top_p or top_k returns a 400, and forced tool use returns an error. Priced at $2/$10 per 1M - the same rate as Sonnet 5 - with cache reads $0.20, 5-minute cache writes $2.50 and 1-hour cache writes $4. Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock (anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5, global profile global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5), Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry (both claude-sonnet-5-5); only the Claude API, Bedrock and OpenRouter routes are modelled here, matching the rest of the Claude family. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/overview

GPT-6.1 Sol: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 point release of the mid-tier Sol model, released September 29, 2026 as the successor to GPT-6 Sol. 1,050,000-token context (922K max input), 128K max output. Reasoning effort low, medium (default), high, xhigh and max; no none or minimal. Structured outputs and streaming supported; tool calling requires the Responses API. Priced at $2/$10 per 1M - the same headline rate as GPT-6 Sol - with cached input at $0.10 (half of GPT-6 Sol's $0.20) and cache writes at $2.50. A prompt above 272K input tokens re-rates the request at $4/$15 (cached $0.20, write $5); that long-context tier is not modelled. Available on the OpenAI API, Amazon Bedrock (openai.gpt-6.1-sol, GA 2026-09-29), Microsoft Foundry and OpenRouter. A GPT-6.1 Sol Pro variant on OpenRouter is not modelled. Sources: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog

Clef: Cloudflare's 27B open-weight decision model (Apache-2.0, released October 1, 2026). It answers Likelihood, Choice (2 to 255 options) and Score (2 to 10 levels) questions, up to 64 in one call, about a state of up to 65,536 tokens, and returns a probability for every allowed option. It writes no text. It takes the same System One request as Jev. Served only on Cloudflare Workers AI, as @cf/cloudflare/clef; Cloudflare reports a median latency of 209 ms. Workers AI also accepts images with the state, which MJ does not send yet. Its raw probabilities are not calibrated to MJ's data, so set thresholds on calibrated values.

Clef-flash: Cloudflare's 9B open-weight decision model (Apache-2.0, released October 1, 2026), the smaller sibling of Clef. It answers Likelihood, Choice (2 to 255 options) and Score (2 to 10 levels) questions, up to 64 in one call, about a state of up to 65,536 tokens, and returns a probability for every allowed option. It writes no text. It takes the same System One request as Jev. Served only on Cloudflare Workers AI, as @cf/cloudflare/clef-flash; Cloudflare reports a median latency of 39 ms. Workers AI also accepts images with the state, which MJ does not send yet. Its raw probabilities are not calibrated to MJ's data, so set thresholds on calibrated values.

rerank-v3.5: Cohere Rerank v3.5 - Semantic reranking model with state-of-the-art performance for English content, optimized for RAG retrieval quality improvement. Decision Reranker: Reranks documents with a typed decision: one call asks a Likelihood question per document ("This note bears on the request"), with the query as the state, and each document's relevance score is the probability. It asks the Default Decision prompt, or the prompt named in the agent's RerankerConfiguration.rerankPromptID, so the decision model and its failover come from that prompt's bindings. It needs no API key of its own. It is not bound to Default Rerank: an agent opts in by setting RerankerConfiguration.rerankerModelId to this model.

Jev: TypeSafe's typed-decision model. It answers Likelihood, Choice (up to 255 options) and Score (2 to 10 levels) questions about a state of up to 32,000 tokens with probabilities, in one call, typically in 70 to 500 ms. It writes no text. Its raw probabilities rank well but are not calibrated to MJ's data, so set thresholds on calibrated values. Reached through OpenRouter's Decisions API, pinned to a dated version.

Kev-0.8B: The 0.8B model of Kev 1.0, Jared Palmer's open-weight (Apache-2.0) family of decision models: a LoRA adapter and a pointer head on Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base. It answers Likelihood, Choice (up to 255 options) and Score (2 to 10 levels) questions with a probability for every allowed option, takes the same System One request as Jev, and writes no text. Each checkpoint ships with a fitted temperature; set thresholds on your own data. Its model card validates states of up to 8,192 tokens. It is the smallest Kev, for when size matters more than accuracy. It is self-hosted: MJ reaches it through the System One Endpoint vendor and the SystemOneDecision driver, at any server with a /v1/systemone route, such as Kev's own server (for example deployed on Modal) or llama.cpp's llama-server, with the endpoint in an API Key with Endpoint credential bound to this model's row.

Kev-4B: The 4B model of Kev 1.0, Jared Palmer's open-weight (Apache-2.0) family of decision models: a LoRA adapter and a pointer head on Qwen3.5-4B-Base. It answers Likelihood, Choice (up to 255 options) and Score (2 to 10 levels) questions with a probability for every allowed option, takes the same System One request as Jev, and writes no text. Each checkpoint ships with a fitted temperature; set thresholds on your own data. Its model card validates states of up to 8,192 tokens. OpenRouter serves it through its Decisions API as jaredpalmer/kev-4b-20260924 (hosted by SiliconFlow in fp8, with an 8,192-token context), reached through the OpenRouterDecision driver. It can also be self-hosted: MJ reaches a self-hosted Kev-4B through the System One Endpoint vendor and the SystemOneDecision driver, at any server with a /v1/systemone route, such as Kev's own server (for example deployed on Modal) or llama.cpp's llama-server, with the endpoint in an API Key with Endpoint credential bound to this model's row.

Kev-9B: The 9B model of Kev 1.0, Jared Palmer's open-weight (Apache-2.0) family of decision models: a LoRA adapter and a pointer head on Qwen3.5-9B-Base. It answers Likelihood, Choice (up to 255 options) and Score (2 to 10 levels) questions with a probability for every allowed option, takes the same System One request as Jev, and writes no text. Each checkpoint ships with a fitted temperature; set thresholds on your own data. Its model card validates states of up to 8,192 tokens. It is self-hosted: MJ reaches it through the System One Endpoint vendor and the SystemOneDecision driver, at any server with a /v1/systemone route, such as Kev's own server (for example deployed on Modal) or llama.cpp's llama-server, with the endpoint in an API Key with Endpoint credential bound to this model's row.

Kev-27B: The 27B model of Kev 1.0, Jared Palmer's open-weight (Apache-2.0) family of decision models: a pointer head on Qwen3.8-27B (Qwen's post-trained release), with every weight fine-tuned, served in bf16 on an 80 GB GPU. It answers Likelihood, Choice (up to 255 options) and Score (2 to 10 levels) questions with a probability for every allowed option, takes the same System One request as Jev, and writes no text. Each checkpoint ships with a fitted temperature; set thresholds on your own data. Its model card validates states of up to 65,536 tokens. It is self-hosted: MJ reaches it through the System One Endpoint vendor and the SystemOneDecision driver, at any server with a /v1/systemone route, such as Kev's own server (for example deployed on Modal) or llama.cpp's llama-server, with the endpoint in an API Key with Endpoint credential bound to this model's row.

LLM Decision: Answers typed decisions (Likelihood, Choice, Score) with a chat model, through the LLM Decision prompt. It is the fallback when no native decision model is available or configured: slower and less consistent than a native decision model, but it needs no extra vendor account.

Perplexity Decider v1 27B: Perplexity's 27B open-weight decision model, pplx-decider-v1-27b (Apache-2.0, released October 1, 2026), fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B. It answers Likelihood, Choice (up to 255 options) and Score (up to 10 levels) questions, up to 128 in one call, about a state of up to 262,144 input tokens (the questions included), and returns a probability for every option or level. It writes no text. It takes the same System One request as Jev. Its only managed host is Perplexity's Decisions API (POST https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/decisions), limited to 10 requests per second per organization; running the open weights yourself needs a CUDA GPU with about 49 GiB for the weights and Perplexity's own Python inference code, which has no HTTP server. Perplexity reports 85.71% accuracy overall on 11 public benchmarks it chose, against 84.51% for Jev, with Jev ahead on 6 of the 11; those are Perplexity's figures, not MJ's measurements. The API also accepts images with the state, which MJ does not send yet. Its raw probabilities are not calibrated to MJ's data, so set thresholds on calibrated values.

AIUsageByModel: Per vendor and model (and currency): model-call count, priced/unpriced run counts, own cost, prompt/completion tokens, median and 95th-percentile latency, and cache efficiency percentage.
AIUsageByScope: Aggregates AI usage facts by PrimaryScopeEntityID and PrimaryScopeRecordID. Supports optional filtering by scope entity, scope record, and date range.
AIUsageByUser: Aggregates AI usage facts by UserID to support user-level chargeback, attribution, and consumption monitoring.

AIUsageCacheEfficiency: Prompt cache efficiency per model and prompt (and currency): cache read volume, cache read share, and estimated savings priced at the token rate in effect when each run executed, with a count of runs that could not be rated.
AIUsageDaily: Primary daily aggregation of AI usage facts. Computes model-call counts, token volumes, latencies (P50/P95), cache reads, and spend (by currency) across all dimensional attributes.
AIUsageErrorRateByModel: Per vendor and model: succeeded, failed and abandoned model calls and the resulting error rate, with cancelled and in-flight runs reported separately.
AIUsageHourly: Primary hourly aggregation of AI usage facts. Computes model-call counts, token volumes, latencies (P50/P95), cache reads, and spend (by currency) across all dimensional attributes.

AIUsageUnpricedAudit: Surfaces completed AI prompt runs where IsPriced = 0 (parallel parents excluded), newest first, with a diagnostic explanation for why each run was unpriced (unmeasured, or missing pricing tier).
Active Users: Returns all active users with basic profile info. Designed as a reusable building block for composed queries.
Recent Entity Changes: Returns recent record changes grouped by entity name. Accepts a lookbackDays parameter to control the time window.
User Activity Summary: Composed query that joins Active Users with Recent Entity Changes to show each user's recent activity level. Demonstrates the {{query:"..."}} composition syntax.

Entity Records By Tag: Returns record IDs for a given entity that have a specific tag assigned, with relevance weight. Composable — join on RecordID to the target entity's primary key to enrich with full record data for tag-based filtering and drill-downs.
ExternalChangeDetection_DetectCreations: Detects new records created in an external system by comparing base view rows to existing MJ record changes.
ExternalChangeDetection_DetectUpdates: Detects updated records in an external system by comparing UpdatedAt timestamps.
ExternalChangeDetection_DetectDeletions: Detects deleted records in an external system by identifying MJ record changes with no matching rows in the base view.

GeoBulkLookup_RecordGeoCodesByEntity: Bulk lookup of all RecordGeoCode rows for a given entity. Returns lightweight fields (ID, RecordID, LocationType, SourceFieldHash, Status) for in-memory staleness checking and existence filtering. Used by ScheduledGeocodingAction to eliminate per-record SQL queries during batch geocoding.

GetAgentRunTree: Returns one row per node of an agent run's complete execution tree: the run, its steps, task graphs those steps submitted, the tasks inside them, and the agent runs those tasks spawned, recursively to a supplied depth cap. Each row carries ParentNodeID/Depth/Sequence so a caller can assemble the tree in memory, plus per-node status, timing, own-cost and own-tokens.

GetArtifactVersionsByID: Returns artifact version fields (name, content mode, file ref, content, mime) joined with the parent artifact and artifact type (including ToolLibraryClass) for a supplied list of ArtifactVersionIDs.

GetConversationArtifactsForAgent: Returns all OUTPUT artifacts with their complete version history and configuration data for a conversation, optionally filtered by the agent that created them. Optimized for AI agent API requests that need to build artifact context.
GetConversationArtifactsMap: Returns a lightweight map of all artifacts linked to conversation messages, without loading full content. Optimized for quick display with lazy-loading support.
GetConversationComplete: Returns complete conversation data in a single query: all messages with their related agent runs and artifacts aggregated as JSON. Optimized for fast conversation loading.

GetConversationsForMemoryManager: Returns all conversation data needed for memory extraction in a single query: conversations with new activity, their details with ratings, and linked agent runs for scope inheritance. Optimized to replace 4 separate sequential queries.

ListConversationDetailFeedbackStats: Aggregate companion for ListConversationDetailFeedback. Returns Total, AvgRating, PositiveCount (>=8), and NegativeCount (<=3) over the same filtered universe (StartDate, EndDate, MinRating, MaxRating, AgentID, SearchText). Used by the Agent Feedback admin page to populate the four stat cards.

ListConversationDetailFeedback: Lists 1-10 user ratings and free-form feedback on conversation messages, joined with the rater (User), conversation, and agent name. Supports time-range, rating-band, and agent filters.

CalculateRunCost: Calculates comprehensive cost metrics for an AI Agent Run, including all nested sub-agent runs. Returns total cost, token usage (input/output), and prompt count by recursively traversing the agent run hierarchy.
RubricDriftPeriodMeans: Mean normalized score per agent, rubric, and criterion for two time windows. Counts only Submitted evaluations that are not self-checks, and only the evaluator's own scores.
Tag Aggregates: Returns per-tag item count and average relevance weight across all tagged items. Used by the Classify dashboard for taxonomy health metrics without loading individual records.

Tag Distribution For Entity: Aggregates tag counts across all records of a given entity, showing how many records have each tag along with average relevance weight and date range. Composable — use as a subquery or join to analyze topic distribution, category breakdowns, and tag popularity.

Tags For Entity Record: Returns all active tags assigned to a specific entity record, including tag hierarchy (parent tag) and relevance weight. Composable — join via RecordID to enrich any entity with its tag metadata.
MJ: AI Actions: List of all actions that are possible across all AI Models
MJ: AI Agent Actions: Table to store the relationship between AI agents and actions.
MJ: AI Agent Artifact Types: Junction table linking AI Agents to the artifact types they can produce. An agent can produce zero to many artifact types.
MJ: AI Agent Categories: Hierarchical organizational grouping for AI agents. Categories form a tree via the ParentID self-referencing foreign key and can carry inherited assignment strategies.

MJ: AI Agent Co Agents: Agent-to-agent affinity registry. Today: OPT-IN co-agent pairings — which underlying agents (or whole agent types) a Realtime-type co-agent can front in live sessions. A co-agent with NO rows is universal (fronts any single agent supplied at runtime — the zero-config default); rows restrict the co-agent to a prebuilt target list. The Type column reserves future relationship natures (Peer/Delegate/Fallback/Reviewer/Observer). Distinct from AIAgentRelationship, which wires agent-to-SUB-AGENT invocation (mappings, message modes); this table is peer affinity with no invocation config.

MJ: AI Agent Configurations: Defines semantic configuration presets for agents, allowing users to select between different AI model configurations (e.g., Fast, Balanced, High Quality) when executing an agent. Each preset maps to an AI Configuration which controls model selection across all prompts.

MJ: AI Agent Credentials: Credentials an agent carries into its harness sandbox, injected as environment variables at session creation. Custody of the secret itself stays in Credential/CredentialEngine - this table records only the GRANT EDGE, in the same reviewable style as AIAgentAction. Distinct from AICredentialBinding, which is inference-selection plumbing for AIPromptRunner failover when MJ itself executes a prompt.
MJ: AI Agent Data Sources: Defines data sources that should be preloaded into the data parameter before agent execution. Supports both RunView and RunQuery sources with configurable caching.

MJ: AI Agent Examples: Stores example input/output pairs for AI agents to learn from successful interactions. Examples are always agent-specific and support optional user/company scoping for personalized examples.

MJ: AI Agent Harnesses: Registry of external agent harnesses this installation can launch as the reasoning substrate for an MJ agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Cline). A row makes a harness AVAILABLE; an agent opts in by naming it in AIAgent.TypeConfiguration. Empty table = no agent can run on a harness, which is the pre-migration behaviour.
MJ: AI Agent Learning Cycles: Tracks the learning cycles for AI Agents where the Agent does offline reasoning, reflection, learning, and updates metadata.

MJ: AI Agent Modalities: Agent-level modality configuration. Allows agents to restrict or customize modality settings beyond what the model supports. Absence of a record means the agent uses model defaults (Text in/out assumed if no records exist).
MJ: AI Agent Models: Table to store the relationship between AI agents and AI models.
MJ: AI Agent Note Types: Defines categories and types for AI agent notes, enabling classification and organization of agent-generated observations, recommendations, and learnings.

MJ: AI Agent Notes: Stores notes, observations, and learnings for AI agents with multi-dimensional scoping (Agent, User, company). Scoping is determined by which FK fields are populated: all NULL = global, AgentID only = agent-specific, UserID only = user-specific across all agents, etc.
MJ: AI Agent Permissions: Defines access control permissions for AI agents using an ACL (Access Control List) model. Permissions can be granted to individual users or roles.
MJ: AI Agent Personas: Configures which personas an AI agent is permitted to wear, their preference order, and which persona serves as the agent's default identity.
MJ: AI Agent Prompts: Links AI agents with the prompts they use, including execution order and context handling.
MJ: AI Agent Relationships: Tracks relationships between AI agents for sub-agent orchestration
MJ: AI Agent Request Types: Lookup table categorizing the types of requests an agent can make to a human (e.g., Approval, Information, Choice, Review, Custom).
MJ: AI Agent Requests: Table to log AI Agent requests, responses, and their statuses.

MJ: AI Agent Rubrics: A rubric an agent publishes for how it should be judged: Evaluation (used by agent eval tests), SelfCheck (the agent checks its own output before returning), or ProductionSampling (a share of real runs is evaluated asynchronously to watch for drift).

MJ: AI Agent Run Steps: Provides basic, step-by-step tracking of agent execution. Each step represents a discrete action within an agent run, such as prompt execution, tool usage, decision making, or sub-agent coordination.

MJ: AI Agent Runs: Tracks individual execution runs of AI agents, including hierarchical sub-agent runs. Provides basic logging, state persistence, and resource tracking for agent executions. Supports pause/resume functionality through state serialization.
MJ: AI Agent Search Scopes: Many-to-many between agents and search scopes, with phase and scheduling control. Drives both pre-execution RAG and agent-invoked scoped search.
MJ: AI Agent Step Paths: Defines paths (edges) between steps in a flow-based AI agent execution graph
MJ: AI Agent Steps: Defines individual steps (nodes) in a flow-based AI agent execution graph

MJ: AI Agent Types: Defines types of AI agents with their system prompts and behavioral characteristics. Each agent type represents a category of agents that share common system-level instructions and capabilities.
MJ: AI Agents: Table to store information about AI agents.
MJ: AI Architectures: Master table of AI model architectures (Transformer, Diffusion, MoE, etc.) for model catalog enrichment and eval reporting.
MJ: AI Configuration Params: Stores configuration parameters that can be referenced by prompts and used to control execution behavior.
MJ: AI Configurations: Stores configurations for AI prompt execution environments and settings.

MJ: AI Credential Bindings: Junction table that binds credentials to AI entities (Vendors, ModelVendors, PromptModels). Decouples credential assignments from core AI entities to prevent MJ updates from overwriting customer configurations. Supports priority-based failover with multiple credentials per binding level.

MJ: AI Modalities: Master list of AI content modalities (Text, Image, Audio, Video, etc.) that models can accept as input or produce as output. New modalities can be added via INSERT without schema changes.
MJ: AI Model Actions: Tracks the actions supported by each AI Model
MJ: AI Model Architectures: Junction table linking AI models to their underlying architectures. Supports multiple architectures per model with ranking.
MJ: AI Model Costs: Stores historical and current pricing information for AI models across different vendors, with optional temporal tracking and support for different processing types

MJ: AI Model Modalities: Junction table linking AI models to their supported input and output modalities with model-specific configuration. Used to extend beyond the default modalities inherited from AIModelType.
MJ: AI Model Personas: Specifies per-model persona availability overrides where a model's supported personas differ from its vendor's default catalog.
MJ: AI Model Price Types: Defines the different types of pricing metrics used by AI model vendors (e.g., Tokens, Minutes, Characters, API Calls)

documents.id: Entity:MJ: AI Model Price Unit Types
documents.text: MJ: AI Model Price Unit Types: Defines the unit scales used for pricing (e.g., Per 1M Tokens, Per 1K Tokens, Per Minute). Includes driver class for normalization calculations
MJ: AI Model Types: Types of AI Models
MJ: AI Model Vendors: Associates AI models with vendors providing them, including vendor-specific implementation details.
MJ: AI Models: Catalog of all AI Models configured in the system
MJ: AI Persona Vendors: Concrete vendor and modality binding for a persona, mapping the abstract persona to a provider-specific wire asset identifier (voice ID or avatar ID).
MJ: AI Personas: Abstract, provider-agnostic presentational identity (voice and/or visual appearance) that AI agents can assume when interacting with users.
MJ: AI Prompt Categories: Categories for organizing AI prompts in a hierarchical structure.
MJ: AI Prompt Models: Associates AI prompts with specific models and configurations, including execution details.
MJ: AI Prompt Runs: Tracks AI prompt executions including timings, inputs, outputs, and performance metrics.
MJ: AI Prompt Types: Types of AI prompts such as Chat, Text-to-Image, Text-to-Video, etc.
MJ: AI Prompts: Stores AI prompts, including references to categories, types, and templates.
MJ: AI Result Cache: Stores cached results of AI prompts, including multiple runs for history and tracking purposes.

MJ: AI Skill Search Scopes: Search Scopes an AI Skill may reach when activated, honoured when AISkill.SearchScopeAccess = 'Assigned'. Mirrors AIAgentSearchScope: Status plus an optional StartAt/EndAt window time-box a grant, and Priority/IsDefault pick among several. An empty table means no skill grants any scope - the pre-migration behaviour.

MJ: AI Usage Types: The base measure a quantity of AI usage is expressed in — Tokens, Seconds, Characters or Images. Referenced by AIModelPriceUnitType (what a billing unit is a quantity of, and therefore what every cost row priced by it measures) and by AIPromptRun (what a recorded quantity counts). Distinct from AIModelPriceUnitType itself, which names the BILLING unit and its scale: audio recorded in Seconds may be billed by the Per Hour unit type.
MJ: AI Vendor Type Definitions: Defines the possible types of AI vendors, such as Model Developer or Inference Provider.
MJ: AI Vendor Types: Associates vendors with their types (Model Developer, Inference Provider) and tracks the status of each role.
MJ: AI Vendors: Stores information about AI vendors providing models and/or inference services.

MJ: API Application Scopes: Defines the scope ceiling for each application with pattern-based rules. Controls which scopes and resource patterns an application can use, regardless of what API keys grant.
MJ: API Applications: Registry of applications that can consume MemberJunction APIs. Each application defines a scope ceiling that limits what API keys can access when used with that application.

MJ: API Key Applications: Optional binding of API keys to specific applications. If no records exist for a key, it works with all applications. If records exist, the key only works with those specific applications.
MJ: API Key Scopes: Junction table linking API keys to their assigned permission scopes. Each key can have multiple scopes, and scopes can be shared across multiple keys.

MJ: API Key Usage Logs: Audit log tracking all API key usage for analytics, debugging, and security monitoring. Records each request including endpoint, response status, timing, and client information.

MJ: API Keys: Stores API keys for programmatic access to MemberJunction services. Keys are stored as SHA-256 hashes for security. Each key is associated with a user context and can have multiple permission scopes assigned.

MJ: API Scopes: Defines reusable permission scopes that can be assigned to API keys. Scopes follow a hierarchical naming convention (e.g., entities:read, agents:execute, admin:*) and are grouped by category for organizational purposes.
MJ: Access Control Rules: Generic ACL-style permission system that can control access to any entity record in the system with granular CRUD permissions.
MJ: Action Authorizations: Links actions to authorizations, one or more of these must be possessed by a user in order to execute the action.
MJ: Action Categories: Organizes actions into categories, including name, description, and optional parent category for hierarchy.
MJ: Action Context Types: Lists possible contexts for action execution with optional descriptions.
MJ: Action Contexts: Links actions to their supported context types enabling a given action to be executable in more than one context.
MJ: Action Execution Logs: Tracks every execution of an action, including start and end times, inputs, outputs, and result codes.

MJ: Action Filters: Defines filters that can be evaluated ahead of executing an action. Action Filters are usable in any code pipeline you can execute them with the same context as the action itself and use the outcome to determine if the action should execute or not.
MJ: Action Libraries: Tracks the list of libraries that a given Action uses, including a list of classes/functions for each library.
MJ: Action Params: Tracks the input and output parameters for Actions.
MJ: Action Result Codes: Defines the possible result codes for each action.
MJ: Actions: Stores action definitions, including prompts, generated code, user comments, and status.
MJ: Application Entities: List of entities within each application. An application can have any number of entities and an entity can be part of any number of applications.

MJ: Application Roles: Controls which roles can access and administer specific applications. When no ApplicationRole records exist for an application, all roles can access it (open access). When at least one record exists, only roles with CanAccess=1 are permitted.
MJ: Application Settings: Stores configuration settings and preferences for applications, including key-value pairs for runtime parameters and user-specific customizations.
MJ: Applications: Applications are used to group entities in the user interface for ease of user access

MJ: Archive Configuration Entities: Per-entity configuration within an archive pipeline. Allows overriding the parent configuration's defaults for mode, retention, batch size, and filtering on a per-entity basis.
MJ: Archive Configurations: Top-level configuration for an archive pipeline. Defines the storage target, default retention policy, archive format, and operational mode for archiving entity records.
MJ: Archive Run Details: Per-record detail for each archive run. Tracks the outcome, storage location, and error information for each individual record processed.
MJ: Archive Runs: Tracks each execution of an archive configuration, including timing, aggregate statistics, and overall status.
MJ: Artifact Permissions: Manages user permissions for artifacts with granular access control (Read, Edit, Delete, Share)
MJ: Artifact Types: Defines the types of artifacts that can be created within conversations
MJ: Artifact Uses: Audit trail of artifact usage for security and analytics. Tracks each time an artifact is viewed, opened, shared, saved, or exported by users.
MJ: Artifact Version Attributes: Stores extracted attribute values from artifact content based on ArtifactType ExtractRules. Prevents re-running extraction logic on every access.
MJ: Artifact Versions: Version history for artifacts, tracking all changes over time
MJ: Artifacts: Independent content items (code, documents, charts) that can be linked to multiple conversations and collections. Supports versioning and sharing.
MJ: Audit Log Types: Defines the types of events that can be recorded in the audit log, enabling categorization and filtering of system activities.
MJ: Audit Logs: Tracks system events and user actions for security, compliance, and debugging purposes, providing a complete audit trail. Any application can write entries to this entity.

MJ: Authentication Providers: Metadata catalog of authentication providers. Each row defines one provider (Auth0, Okta, MSAL, Cognito, Google, WorkOS, or any third-party driver) whose implementation is resolved at runtime from DriverClass via MJGlobal.ClassFactory.CreateInstance(BaseAuthProvider, DriverClass). Supersedes the hard-wired mj.config.cjs authProviders array, which remains a back-compat fallback when this table is empty.
MJ: Authorization Roles: Links authorizations to roles, defining which permissions are granted to users assigned to specific roles in the system.
MJ: Authorizations: Stores the fundamental permissions and access rights that can be granted to users and roles throughout the system.

MJ: Cluster Analysis: A saved cluster analysis: the configuration, computed metrics, and projected 2D/3D layout of a clustering run over an entity's embedding vectors. First-class, queryable, and shareable — replaces the prior approach of stashing analyses in a User Settings JSON blob / browser localStorage. Owner-private; explicit shares are recorded in ResourcePermission against the "Cluster Analysis" ResourceType.

MJ: Cluster Analysis Clusters: One named cluster within a saved ClusterAnalysis. Holds the cluster's label (LLM-generated or user-edited), member count, and display color, so labels can be regenerated or hand-edited per cluster without re-running the whole analysis.
MJ: Collection Artifacts: Links collections to specific artifact versions. Each collection can contain multiple versions of the same artifact.
MJ: Collection Permissions: Manages sharing permissions for collections, allowing granular access control
MJ: Collections: Organizational folders for storing and categorizing artifacts. Supports nested folder structure for hierarchical organization.
MJ: Communication Base Message Types: Base message types and their supported functionalities.
MJ: Communication Logs: Logs of sent and received messages.
MJ: Communication Provider Message Types: Providers and their supported message types with additional attributes.
MJ: Communication Providers: All supported communication providers.
MJ: Communication Runs: Runs of bulk message sends and receives.

MJ: Companies: A list of organizational units within your business. These can be subsidiaries or divisions or other units. Companies are used to organizae employee records and also for separating integrations if you have multiple integrations of the same type of system.
MJ: Company Integration Entity Maps: Maps an external object from a company integration to a MemberJunction entity, controlling sync direction, matching, and conflict resolution.
MJ: Company Integration Field Maps: Maps individual fields between an external source object and a MemberJunction entity, with optional transform pipeline.
MJ: Company Integration Record Maps: Maps records between internal entities and external system identifiers, maintaining synchronization between MemberJunction and integrated platforms.

documents.id: Entity:MJ: Company Integration Run API Logs
documents.text: MJ: Company Integration Run API Logs: Logs detailed API calls and responses during integration runs, including request/response payloads, status codes, and timing information.
